Workday Or Autodesk: Is The Louder AI Story The Better Stock?
If you own Workday (WDAY) or Autodesk (ADSK), you hold the same bet: the company that already keeps a customer's data gets paid as that customer adopts AI. Workday keeps HR and finance records, and Autodesk keeps design, manufacturing, and construction data.
Workday puts a dollar figure on its AI sales, yet its early fiscal 2028 target calls for slower growth. Autodesk reports no separate AI revenue and grew faster over the past year.
Did Workday And Autodesk Raise Their Outlooks For The Same Reason?
Both raised guidance at their fiscal Q2 2027 reports. Workday lifted its fiscal 2027 subscription revenue outlook by just 0.1%. Its early fiscal 2028 target is about 11% subscription growth, down from the 13% it guides for fiscal 2027.
Autodesk raised its fiscal 2027 total revenue outlook by 1.6%. The raise includes MaintainX, a high-growth business it recently bought, plus a stronger second quarter. Its AI task automation comes built into some subscriptions, and management says it lifts growth at Fusion, its design and manufacturing software. So the raises share a cause but not a source: both followed second-quarter beats, but Autodesk's also folds in the MaintainX acquisition, while Workday's reflects execution alone.
Workday's AI is real, but its newest products are slow to pay. Its AI products carry nearly $600 million of annual recurring revenue. Many of its new AI products are billed through flex credits, and the CEO expects that revenue months or a year down the road. Just over 200 customers had signed up for flex credits, against more than 5,500 using Workday's built-in agents.
What Are You Paying For In Workday While You Wait?
You pay more for Workday. Its price-to-EBIT multiple is 33.0, against 21.1 for Autodesk. That premium comes while flex-credit revenue has not yet shown up. The CFO says the fiscal 2028 target leaves out part of its AI momentum, and sees upside there.
Workday also gives strategic customers Sana Enterprise, its AI workbench, free for a year. A Workday holder is betting that free use turns into subscription revenue growth.
How Does Autodesk Make Its Money?
Autodesk sells subscriptions to software such as Fusion and Autodesk Forma. Over the last twelve months, its revenue grew 17.9%, against 13.3% for Workday. Its GAAP operating margin over the last twelve months was 27.9%, more than twice Workday's 12.0%.
MaintainX was not profitable when Autodesk bought it, and the CFO says it dilutes adjusted operating margin in fiscal 2027, though Autodesk kept that margin outlook unchanged.
Which Of The Two Holds Up Better On The Numbers?
Autodesk, clearly. It is cheaper, grew faster over the past year, and is far more profitable. Workday's edge on the business is its three-year growth record, and that is close to a tie: revenue growth averaged 14.8% a year over three years, against 14.4% for Autodesk.
That near-tie matters because Autodesk's recent pace includes a boost from its new transaction model, worth about 1.5 percentage points of fiscal 2027 revenue growth, that the CFO says will not recur in fiscal 2028. The case for Workday improves if flex credits lift subscription growth above its fiscal 2028 target. Workday Unifies Workforce Management, HR, and Payroll on One AI Platform for Smarter Frontline Work
PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), the enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT, has been named a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant™ for Workforce Management Technology. A complimentary copy of the report is available here.
Frontline work happens on the floor, in the warehouse, and behind the counter, not in a back office. Workday's workforce management suite brings time tracking, absence management, scheduling, and labor optimization together within Workday Human Capital Management (HCM). This gives frontline leaders one system to manage labor costs, compliance, schedules, and time while giving workers and managers mobile-friendly tools they can use on the go.
"For too long, frontline teams were asked to use technology designed for desk work, not the pace of the floor, the warehouse, or the counter," said David Wachtel, general manager, Workday HCM. "Workday puts that workforce first, with tools that are simple to use and AI that takes the busywork off their plate."
One AI Platform Built for the Way Frontline Teams Work
Workday's workforce management suite is built for the industries where frontline work happens, from retail and manufacturing to hospitality and grocery, and beyond. Capabilities like demand forecasting allow teams to plan ahead and staff to real demand rather than guessing, with AI that reads patterns across seasonality, events, and historical trends to match the right people to the right shifts.
Workday also meets workers where they are, with mobile, web, and kiosk options to clock in. Since schedules, time off, pay, shift swaps, and preferences all live in one place, setting availability or picking up an open shift takes just a few taps.
AI Agents That Give Time Back to Your People
Workday's workforce management suite includes agentic capabilities powered by Sana, Workday's agentic experience, that automates time-consuming tasks, freeing managers and workers to trade desk time for face time.
The Workforce Management Agent automates schedule changes, time tracking, shift swaps, and demand-based staffing, and applies Workday policies, knowledge, and organizational data to optimize scheduling decisions and route approvals according to its configured rules. For example, Workday customers using the Workforce Management Agent in early adoption saw up to a 90% reduction in the time spent managing shift schedule changes, a 65% improvement in process automation on average, and a 75% reduction in manual time entry errors.
With Workday's workforce management suite, automotive services retailer Valvoline cut the time its managers spend generating weekly schedules from more than two hours to about 15 minutes, freeing them to focus on coaching and customers instead of paperwork.
Health and fitness company Life Time hit 95% mobile app adoption after rolling out Workday Scheduling, handing workers real self-service control over their schedules and time. Life Time's managers saved over 50,000 hours each year, and Life Time realized $1 million in annual labor savings and a 50% reduction in overtime costs.

Workday (WDAY) Stock Dips After Announcing 500 Job Cuts in Latest Restructuring
By Trader EdgeSeptember 30, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
Approximately 500 positions eliminated, representing 2.5% of total headcount.
Product and Technology divisions bear the brunt of workforce reductions.
Expected restructuring expenses range from $65M to $85M.
Second workforce reduction announced by Workday in 2026, following February cuts.
Shares have declined approximately 12% since the start of the year.
Workday (WDAY) stock edged higher by 0.30% during Tuesday trading despite the company announcing another wave of workforce reductions. The enterprise cloud applications provider is eliminating approximately 500 positions, representing roughly 2.5% of its total employee base worldwide.
The layoffs were revealed through an 8-K filing submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The majority of impacted positions are concentrated in the company’s Product and Technology organization.
According to the filing, the decision aims to “better align team structures with Workday’s strategic growth priorities.” The company also noted it would reduce certain leased office facilities.
With approximately 21,000 employees on the payroll as of late January, the 2.5% reduction translates to around 525 individuals facing job elimination.
The workforce reduction carries substantial financial implications. Workday anticipates incurring between $65M and $85M in restructuring-related charges.
The bulk of these expenses, ranging from $55M to $70M, will be recorded during the third quarter of fiscal year 2027. An additional $10M is slated for recognition in the fourth quarter.
Employee-related costs, including severance packages and benefits, account for $40M to $55M of the total expense. Stock-based compensation charges contribute roughly $10M more.
The remaining $15M stems from impairment charges related to office space the company plans to vacate. All these costs represent either non-cash items or one-time expenses directly connected to the restructuring initiative.
The financial burden will also impact profitability metrics. Workday projects its GAAP operating margin will trail its non-GAAP counterpart by approximately 21 percentage points during Q3.
Over the complete fiscal year, this differential is expected to tighten to roughly 19 percentage points. The company’s November 27 third-quarter earnings release will provide comprehensive details.
This marks Workday’s second round of job eliminations in 2026. The company previously reduced headcount by approximately 2% in February, with those cuts primarily affecting the Global Customer Operations division.
That initial reduction was followed by unexpected leadership changes. Approximately one week after the February announcement, then-CEO Carl Eschenbach departed from his role.
Company cofounder Aneel Bhusri assumed the CEO position, marking his fourth stint leading the organization. Bhusri has maintained an optimistic public stance regarding Workday’s competitive positioning.
Notably, neither workforce reduction this year explicitly referenced artificial intelligence as a contributing factor. This distinction carries significance amid widespread concerns about AI’s impact on software companies throughout 2026.
Market participants became increasingly anxious earlier this year about the possibility of enterprises leveraging AI to develop internal software solutions rather than purchasing commercial platforms. This concern, dubbed the “SaaSpocalypse,” erased hundreds of billions in market capitalization from software sector companies.
Bhusri directly addressed these worries during Workday’s August quarterly earnings discussion. He stated he had encountered zero customers considering replacing Workday with internally developed or startup alternatives, and this remained true in subsequent quarters.
Nevertheless, share price performance reveals a challenging period. Workday stock has retreated approximately 12% since the beginning of the year.
The company indicated it intends to continue recruiting for specific strategic positions and geographic markets throughout fiscal 2027. This selective hiring will occur concurrently with the workforce reductions disclosed this week.
Workday’s November 27 third-quarter financial results will serve as an important checkpoint. The report should clarify whether the restructuring expenses and profitability impacts materialize as management anticipates.

New AI Solution Makes it Simpler for Employers to Manage Benefits and Easier for Employees to Actually Use Them
Workday Also Introduces Benefits Guidance Through Self-Service Agent to Help Employees Get Clear, Personal Answers About Their Benefits
PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), the enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT, today announced Workday Total Benefits, a new AI solution designed to bring everything connected to an employee's benefits into one experience. Instead of juggling separate providers and logins, employees get one simple way to find and use the benefits they already have. For organizations, it helps automate benefits administration by bringing employers and benefits providers together in a seamless system.
Workday Launches Total Benefits, Bringing Health, Wealth, and Wellbeing Support Together in One Place
Benefits are one of the biggest investments a company makes in its people. That investment keeps growing: employers expect a median 9% rise in health care costs in 2026, one of the steepest increases yet. And the technology behind these investments is often scattered across a growing number of provider systems, which drives up costs, makes it hard for leaders to see what's working, and leaves employees confused about what they even have.
Workday Total Benefits is made up of four parts that work together:
Workday Wellness streamlines benefits administration by connecting a company's benefits providers directly to Workday, automating plan setup and enabling financial, absence, and insurance election data to flow to providers in real time..
Benefits Guidance through Self-Service Agent answers employees' benefits questions in plain language, through open enrollment and major life moments, from welcoming a new baby to everyday decisions in between, so they get the full value of their benefits.
Life and Money Solutions offers support for employees' personal and financial needs, like getting access to earned wages early or verifying income for a loan, through trusted partners.
Benefits Administration Services brings in extra, hands-on help from partners for HR teams that want support running their programs day to day.
Workday Total Benefits turns benefits from something employees have to search for into something that finds them, proactively surfacing recommended providers at enrollment, a life event, or any moment in between.
"Benefits have become incredibly complicated for organizations to manage and too difficult for employees to understand, leaving many unaware of the support available to them," said David Wachtel, general manager, core HR products, Workday. "Workday Total Benefits uses technology and a strong ecosystem of partners to fix that — bringing benefits, data, and guidance together so companies can simplify how they manage benefits and employees can easily find and use the support that's right for them."
Workday Wellness: Connecting the Benefits Ecosystem to Power Automation and Real-Time AI Insights
At the center of Workday Total Benefits is Workday Wellness, which is now available to U.S. customers. Workday Wellness is an AI solution that will allow HR and benefits leaders to see, in real time, which benefits employees are using, how programs are performing, and where costs are heading.
Workday Wellness connects benefits providers directly to Workday, so benefits implementations are streamlined and administration runs automatically across systems. For example, early adopter customers saw a 75% reduction in time spent onboarding a new benefit provider.
Workday Wellness's ecosystem of providers keeps growing. New partners including Bright Horizons, Care.com, Empower, EyeMed, Maven Clinic, Morgan Stanley at Work, Multiply, Oura Ring, SmithRx, WEX, and When have joined the platform. Leading brokers and advisors, including Aon, are on Workday now too, so they can work directly with benefits leaders.
"Employees don't lack benefits, they lack a way to find and use what's already offered to them," said Tanner Brunsdale, director of benefits and mobility, Lyft. "Workday Wellness helps us close the gap between what we're paying for and what people actually use, by surfacing the right benefit to the right person at exactly the moment they need it."
Self-Service Agent Gives Employees Clear, Personal Guidance on Their Benefits
Workday also introduced benefits guidance through its Self-Service Agent, helping employees understand and use the benefits they already have, in plain language, without needing to be an HR expert.
For example, an employee can use the Self-Service to describe what's going on in their own words, such as "I'm having a baby," or "My spouse just lost coverage," or "Which plan should I pick this year?" The agent explains the options, compares plans side by side, and helps them take the next step, like enrolling in coverage, adding a dependent, or updating a beneficiary. It also flags relevant programs and reminders throughout the year, not just at enrollment.
Life and Money Solutions Bring Everyday Support to Employees
Workday Total Benefits also includes Life and Money Solutions, a set of partner-powered capabilities that help employees manage personal and financial needs connected to their pay and their job.
Enhancing direct deposit. Employees can now open or connect an account with financial providers, including OnePay, EarnIn, PayPal, Cash App, and Chime, to receive their paycheck and access additional financial services.
Access earned wages. Through DailyPay, eligible employees have the flexibility to access the money they've already earned before their scheduled payday.
Verifying income and employment. Employees often need to prove where they work and what they earn, for an apartment, a loan, or a government service. Workday helps make the process easier for HR by connecting and automating requests through providers like The Work Number by Equifax, Experian®, and Checkr, so people aren't stuck chasing down paperwork themselves.
These solutions are built for the practical, everyday things that affect an employee's financial confidence and free up their time. Companies can choose which solutions make the most sense for their workforce.
Workday Now Offers Benefits Administration Services
For companies that want additional help running their benefits programs, Workday Total Benefits includes benefits administration services for customers.
Through partners including Strada and Benefit Harbor, companies can get expert support for day-to-day benefits work — such as migrating from legacy benefits systems, configuring plans, and managing ongoing administration — reducing the workload on HR teams while keeping everything connected to the data and workflows they already use in Workday.
"Too often, benefits administration is more complex than it needs to be for both employers and employees. By bringing together Workday's technology and Strada's operational expertise, we're helping organizations create a simpler, more connected benefits experience," said Frank Leistner, SVP of global partnerships at Strada.
Workday Wellness is now generally available for U.S. customers.
Benefits guidance through Self-Service Agent is expected to become generally available in October 2026.
Benefits Administration Services are now generally available.
Life and Money Solutions are now generally available for customers in the U.S. The Equifax integration is available today, additional integrations with Experian and Checkr are expected to become available in late October 2026.
To learn more about AI's impact on benefits, read the Workday blog.
Workday operates at the heart of the enterprise – HR, finance, and IT – where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, and trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists with work to agents that are capable of driving measurable outcomes. Workday Launches in the UAE to Help Organisations Transform HR, Finance, and IT in the AI Era
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:28 AM PDT 5 min read
New Dubai Office, Expanded Local Leadership, and Fresh Research Signal Workday's Long-Term Commitment as AI Adoption Accelerates Across the UAE
DUBAI, UAE, Oct. 1, 2026/PRNewswire/ -- Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), the enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT, announced the launch of its operations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). To mark the launch, Workday released new findings from its report "Beyond Productivity: Measuring the Real Value of AI in the UAE," which explores how organisations are measuring AI's impact not just through time savings, but through the value it creates for people and the business.
From L to R: Angelique de Vries-Schipperijn and Zakaria Haltout at Workday launch in the UAE
The research found that AI adoption in the UAE has reached a major milestone, with 90% of employees using it at least weekly, including 58% who use it multiple times a week and 18% who use it every working day. Employees report saving an average of 3.6 hours a week through AI, while more than half of directors and C-suite executives are using AI every week.
The UAE launch is anchored by a new office in Dubai, dedicated regional operations, and expanded local leadership, creating a local hub to engage directly with customers, build strong partnerships, and attract top local talent. The investment positions Workday to help organisations modernise HR and finance, manage change, and get more value from AI as they support the UAE's national transformation goals.
Workday convened senior leaders including Angelique De Vries-Schipperijn, President, EMEA, and Zakaria Haltout, Group Vice President (GVP), Middle East, Turkey & Africa (META) to mark the opening.
A Region Ready for Its Next Stage of Growth
The Middle East is a cornerstone of Workday's global growth strategy, as strong customer demand, growing cloud adoption, and national transformation agendas make this an increasingly important market. Momentum is building across both the public and private sectors, and the organisations that modernise now will set the pace for the years ahead.
"The UAE is a key market in Workday's growth strategy, with organisations pursuing transformation against some of the world's most ambitious national agendas," said Angelique De Vries-Schipperijn, President, EMEA, Workday. "To succeed, they need technology that helps them move faster, adopt new ways of working, and show clear results while maintaining the trust and control large, regulated organisations require."
AI Adoption Is Creating New Opportunities, But Human Oversight Remains Critical
While AI adoption continues to accelerate across the UAE, the research found that realising its full value still depends on human oversight, trust, and continued investment in skills. Employees spend an average of 3.4 hours per week clarifying, correcting, or rewriting low-quality AI-generated outputs, highlighting the continued importance of people, clear rules, and careful review.
Crucially, UAE organisations are reinvesting AI gains in their people rather than focusing solely on cost reduction:
33% use AI-enabled efficiencies to handle greater workloads without increasing headcount.
32% are directing time and cost savings created by AI toward training, upskilling, and reskilling.
Another 32% are channeling AI-driven efficiencies into workload management, workplace flexibility, and employee well-being.
Only 24% say time and cost savings created by AI are primarily being used for cost reduction.
Just 0.2% of respondents said AI has not generated meaningful time or cost savings.
"Organisations across the UAE are moving from AI experimentation to everyday use, with 90% of employees using AI at least weekly," said Zakaria Haltout, GVP, META, Workday. "But lasting value depends on trust, human oversight, and continued investment in skills, which is why Workday helps organisations bring AI into the flow of work with the context, guardrails, and trusted processes they need to move forward with confidence."
Workday operates at the heart of the enterprise, HR, finance, and IT – where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, and trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work and drive measurable outcomes. Mon, September 28, 2026 at 8:07 AM PDT 3 min read
Named a Workday Partner, Teem integrates with Workday Strategic Sourcing and Workday Contract Lifecycle Management to help joint customers discover the right suppliers faster and stop redundant spend before it happens
SAN DIEGO, September 28, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Teem Finance, Inc., an AI-native procurement intelligence company, today announced a partnership with Workday to integrate its advanced supplier insights with Workday Strategic Sourcing and Workday Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM). This partnership enables Workday Spend Management customers to leverage AI for faster, better-informed supplier decisions while automatically flagging redundant purchases before they happen.
Teem automates the research and analysis that traditionally consumes weeks of manual effort for enterprise procurement teams:
Category Management: Consolidates contracts, evaluations, and market research into an evidence-backed view complete with spend breakdowns, renewal calendars, and actionable recommendations to "Invest", "Tolerate", "Migrate" or "Eliminate".
Supplier Discovery: Turns plain-language requests into structured recommendations by checking what a company already owns, then ranking qualified market alternatives through side-by-side comparisons.
Customers have used these capabilities to reduce redundant software spend by 20% to 35% and cut sourcing cycle times in half.
The integration with Workday Strategic Sourcing and Workday CLM allows existing Workday customers to experience the power of Teem's supplier intelligence in a turnkey way. Supplier and contract context flows directly from Workday into Teem, so recommendations reflect the supplier base a customer already has, with no manual data loading required.
In addition, Workday Strategic Sourcing integration leverages Teem data to help power supplier discovery and cost deflection use cases directly. The cost deflection use case helps prevent bad spend from happening in the first place by analyzing new purchase requests and upcoming renewals against the capabilities that already exist within a company's supplier catalog, flagging overlap before a new purchase is made.
As a Workday Partner, Teem will bring to the Workday ecosystem:
AI-powered supplier research and discovery at the front of the sourcing process, surfacing qualified suppliers against both the existing supplier base and the broader market.
Cost deflection guardrails that flag what a company already owns before it buys something new, helping cut redundant tools and overlapping spend.
Category management intelligence, including portfolio analysis, application rationalization, and data-backed recommendations to reduce total cost of ownership.
Faster, data-backed evaluations through side-by-side product comparisons and stakeholder surveys that capture requirements without a heavy RFx.
"Procurement teams are being asked to control costs and move faster at the same time, and the answer is not more manual analysis," said Ben Mappen, founder and CEO of Teem. "By connecting Teem with Workday Strategic Sourcing and Workday CLM, joint customers can see what they already own, discover the right suppliers in minutes instead of weeks, and stop redundant spend before a purchase order is ever created. Workday runs the systems where supplier decisions happen, and that makes it the natural place for this intelligence to live."
Teem will host a session at Workday Rising, Oct. 12-15 in Las Vegas: "Turn Supplier Intelligence into Savings with Workday Strategic Sourcing and Teem." Registration is open at rising.workday.com.
Teem is an AI-native procurement intelligence platform that helps enterprises automate category management, supplier discovery, and vendor consolidation. Teem's agentic AI delivers instant insight across business fit, product overlap, and supplier capabilities, so procurement teams can make faster, smarter decisions and eliminate redundant spend. Mon, September 28, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 2 min read
New Workday Cloud Connect for Learning integration automatically synchronizes training records and keeps content up-to-date, reducing administrative effort
TAMPA BAY, Fla., September 28, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--KnowBe4, a cybersecurity company specializing in digital workforce security, securing both AI agents and humans, today announced it has launched KnowBe4 for Workday Learning, a Workday Cloud Connect for Learning (CCL) integration. The integration enables organizations to deliver KnowBe4 security awareness and compliance training seamlessly through Workday Learning while automatically synchronizing records to reduce administrative overhead. As a Workday Innovation Partner, KnowBe4 has achieved the Workday Design Approved Integration badge.
KnowBe4 for Workday Learning connects KnowBe4's training library directly with Workday Learning, powered by Sana, giving organizations a streamlined way to manage security awareness training from within their existing learning ecosystem. With a single integration, customers can keep training content current, eliminate manual record reconciliation and maintain accurate, real-time training data within Workday Learning.
Key capabilities include:
Real-time training record synchronization: KnowBe4 training activity and completion records are automatically updated in Workday Learning in near real time, helping organizations maintain accurate, audit-ready transcripts.
Native catalog syncing: KnowBe4's training content catalog is integrated directly into the Workday Learning content picker and synced five days a week to help ensure organizations always have access to the latest training content.
Seamless SSO access: Single sign-on from Workday to KnowBe4 lets learners launch training directly from their Workday dashboard, helping reduce dropoff caused by separate logins or portals.
"As organizations manage a digital workforce security program that includes both humans and AI agents, security awareness and compliance programs need to be effective without becoming operationally complex," said Greg Kras, chief product officer at KnowBe4. "KnowBe4 content being delivered via Workday Learning helps organizations streamline how they deliver training while helping ensure completion records remain accurate and up to date within Workday Learning. By reducing manual effort and improving data integrity, organizations can spend less time managing records and more time strengthening the security of their digital workforce."
This integration is available to customers on KnowBe4 Attack Simulation & Training offers including Diamond, Training-Only Diamond, SAT Advanced subscriptions and Workday Learning with the CCL SKU.
More information on KnowBe4's integration can be found on the Workday Marketplace, which provides easy access to solutions built by Workday and its partners.
KnowBe4 empowers the modern workforce to make smarter security decisions every day. Trusted by more than 70,000 organizations worldwide, KnowBe4 provides digital workforce security, securing both AI agents and humans. The KnowBe4 Platform provides attack simulation and training, collaboration security, and agent security powered by AIDA (Artificial Intelligence Defense Agents) and a proprietary Risk Score. The platform leverages 15-years of behavioral data to combat advanced threats including social engineering, prompt injection, and shadow AI. By securing humans and agents, KnowBe4 helps organizations strengthen workforce trust and defense. More info at knowbe4.com.

Workday, Inc. WDAY has launched Total Benefits, a new artificial intelligence (AI)-powered solution that brings employees' health, financial and wellbeing programs together in one place. The solution aims to simplify administration for employers while helping employees better understand and make use of the offerings available to them.
Workday Total Benefits combines four key capabilities, including Workday Wellness, Benefits Guidance through Self-Service Agent, Life and Money Solutions, and Benefits Administration Services. By combining AI, automation and partner support, Workday is making benefits management simpler and more connected for both employers and employees.

Block XYZ is expanding the reach of its two major ecosystems, Square and Cash App, through separate integrations with Apple and Workday. Square has introduced an Apple Business integration that allows eligible sellers to manage and synchronize their business information across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet and other Apple services directly from Square Dashboard. Separately, Cash App has partnered with Workday to simplify direct deposit enrollment for U.S. employees, strengthening its push to become a primary financial platform for modern earners.
The Apple Business integration is designed to enhance Square sellers' visibility and reduce the operational burden of maintaining business listings across multiple channels. Sellers can manage branding, logos, operating hours, addresses and phone numbers through Square Dashboard, with updates automatically synchronized across connected Apple services. Businesses can also add action links for ordering, pickup, delivery, bookings or appointments directly to their Apple Maps place cards, potentially converting customer discovery into transactions. Square noted that claimed Apple Maps locations receive 30% more views, while action links have generated 31% higher click-through rates across website, call and other action buttons.
The integration is available across Square's eight supported markets, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, and complements Square's broader strategy of helping merchants get discovered across emerging customer channels. The company has also recently integrated with AI platforms such as ChatGPT and Claude.
Cash App's partnership with Workday will enable eligible U.S. employees to select Cash App as their direct deposit destination through Workday's Enhanced Direct Deposit experience beginning Oct. 1. Given Workday's reach across millions of U.S. employees, the integration provides Cash App with another distribution channel to attract paycheck deposits and deepen customer engagement. Cash App had 9.4 million Primary Banking Actives in the second quarter of 2026, up 17% year over year, indicating continued traction among customers using the platform for broader banking and money-management needs.
Together, the Apple and Workday partnerships highlight Block's strategy of embedding its products into widely used consumer and enterprise platforms. The Apple integration could help Square improve merchant engagement and transaction opportunities by linking business discovery more directly with commerce, while the Workday partnership may support Cash App's efforts to attract higher-quality, more engaged banking customers through direct deposit. Over time, deeper integrations across both ecosystems could support increased customer retention, transaction volumes and monetization opportunities for Block.

The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees meets in the Robert J. Higgins Welcome Center on Upper College Road on the Kingston campus. (URI photo)
A colossal software overhaul of the University of Rhode Island's (URI) administrative and payroll systems on track to launch next fall may need to change course after state officials asked university officials to possibly take over a big responsibility it previously told them not to pursue.
URI began its transition to a more modern infrastructure for its finance, human resources, payroll, budgeting, and faculty administration systems in January. Based around the Workday platform — the same software used by the state of Rhode Island to administer its payroll — the project is about halfway complete and is expected to launch in October 2027.
Abby Benson, URI's vice president for administration and finance, told trustees during a Sept. 14 Finance and Facilities Committee meeting that the school has always managed its own administrative systems while still relying on the state for payroll.
But before the project began, URI had asked the state whether it should assume payroll processing duties for the university's full-time employees — a decision URI needed to make early in the planning phase, so it would know whether to build around payroll or not.
"We had asked them that question explicitly a year ago, and they said no," Benson told trustees.
After the trustees reviewed an outline of the Workday plans last November, URI embarked on its lengthy modernization process. It left payroll processing for its full-time employees to the state's own Workday system, which experienced numerous problems after it debuted late last year.
The state's Workday-based ERP rollout cost approximately $99 million and was completed late last year, with the firm Accenture responsible for the system's implementation. The state's transition from its older, often analog payroll system has led to paychecks with incorrect wages, overtime, holiday pay, benefits or deductions. There were also mislabeled W-2s which led to some state employees having to amend their tax filings multiple times during the height of tax season.
Earlier this month, the Department of Administration also attributed an almost yearlong lapse in updates to the state's online payroll transparency portal to the ERP switchover. The portal, which provides easy lookup of any state employee's wage and salary information, has not been updated since October 2025.
URI and state leaders meet once a month to discuss the school's own Workday project. Recently, Benson told trustees, the university started talks with the state to determine whether the school should assume the payroll functions its system was not expecting to fulfill.
State officials have been "good partners," Benson said. But the symbiotic relationship between the two payroll systems has generated some concern for the university, Benson suggested at the meeting: "I can't say that there won't be issues on the state side, just like there are issues on the state side now."
This new set of potential demands on URI's Workday timeline, Benson warned, could have "significant monetary and project schedule impacts" for the school. Benson told the trustees on Sept. 14 that the school was meeting with state officials later that week to continue discussing the two Workday systems.
On Tuesday, about two weeks after that trustees meeting, Benson wrote in an email to Rhode Island Current that URI and the state are still "closely collaborating" to determine the best ways for their newly-designed enterprise resource planning, or ERP, infrastructure to live in harmony. Both systems, Benson wrote, "involve dependencies required for successful implementation."
"We are actively exploring with the State the best approach to address these dependencies," Benson wrote. Asked whether that includes the possibility of URI administering payroll in-house, she added, "We're looking at several options, including that one."
The Department of Administration, meanwhile, declined to comment on any discussions taking place.
"While we don't comment on internal discussions and defer any specific questions about URI's project to the university, the State is fully supportive of URI's Workday implementation project," department spokesperson Karen Greco wrote in an email. "The State team's specific role in this is to ensure the integration with the State system is secure, efficient and meeting the necessary requirements to achieve mutual success."
Stephanie Cavanaugh, URI's Workday program director, told trustees on Sept. 14 that the new platform will replace URI's PeopleSoft-based human resources and finance systems, as well as the school's current budgeting software. The school's student information system is staying put and will integrate with Workday.
Currently, URI's full-time employees, including those eligible for benefits, are paid via the state's payroll system. URI's internal systems handle the remainder of the university's workforce, which includes several thousand part-time and non-benefit employees.
The new system is designed to track time for full-time employees while still sending payroll data to the state, which would continue processing paychecks.
"Any problem that the state has with their payroll system impacts our employees, and we've been managing and mitigating that for the last six months," Benson told the Finance Committee. She suggested the state had revived the possibility of URI handling payroll "based on some of the challenges on their end."
Benson reiterated that the problem was not the Workday software per se, which she called "a great system," but its configuration.
"It has to do with how the software was configured," she said. "There's a lot of factors that go into this. There's the software itself, and there's the group that you use to help you implement the software and how you design the software, and that's the process we're in right now."
Cavanaugh said the university's Workday project is "generally…in a good place," and the project remains on schedule, but added, "We cannot vary too much from that schedule and from the scope we're currently on to maintain the current budget status."
Functional teams working on the school's ERP effort continue to meet weekly, she said, and the university is planning a lengthy testing period, from December 2026 to August 2027, to prepare for launch next fall.

Workday Or Autodesk: Is The Louder AI Story The Better Stock?
If you own Workday (WDAY) or Autodesk (ADSK), you hold the same bet: the company that already keeps a customer's data gets paid as that customer adopts AI. Workday keeps HR and finance records, and Autodesk keeps design, manufacturing, and construction data.
Workday puts a dollar figure on its AI sales, yet its early fiscal 2028 target calls for slower growth. Autodesk reports no separate AI revenue and grew faster over the past year.
Did Workday And Autodesk Raise Their Outlooks For The Same Reason?
Both raised guidance at their fiscal Q2 2027 reports. Workday lifted its fiscal 2027 subscription revenue outlook by just 0.1%. Its early fiscal 2028 target is about 11% subscription growth, down from the 13% it guides for fiscal 2027.
Autodesk raised its fiscal 2027 total revenue outlook by 1.6%. The raise includes MaintainX, a high-growth business it recently bought, plus a stronger second quarter. Its AI task automation comes built into some subscriptions, and management says it lifts growth at Fusion, its design and manufacturing software. So the raises share a cause but not a source: both followed second-quarter beats, but Autodesk's also folds in the MaintainX acquisition, while Workday's reflects execution alone.
Workday's AI is real, but its newest products are slow to pay. Its AI products carry nearly $600 million of annual recurring revenue. Many of its new AI products are billed through flex credits, and the CEO expects that revenue months or a year down the road. Just over 200 customers had signed up for flex credits, against more than 5,500 using Workday's built-in agents.
What Are You Paying For In Workday While You Wait?
You pay more for Workday. Its price-to-EBIT multiple is 33.0, against 21.1 for Autodesk. That premium comes while flex-credit revenue has not yet shown up. The CFO says the fiscal 2028 target leaves out part of its AI momentum, and sees upside there.
Workday also gives strategic customers Sana Enterprise, its AI workbench, free for a year. A Workday holder is betting that free use turns into subscription revenue growth.
How Does Autodesk Make Its Money?
Autodesk sells subscriptions to software such as Fusion and Autodesk Forma. Over the last twelve months, its revenue grew 17.9%, against 13.3% for Workday. Its GAAP operating margin over the last twelve months was 27.9%, more than twice Workday's 12.0%.
MaintainX was not profitable when Autodesk bought it, and the CFO says it dilutes adjusted operating margin in fiscal 2027, though Autodesk kept that margin outlook unchanged.
Which Of The Two Holds Up Better On The Numbers?
Autodesk, clearly. It is cheaper, grew faster over the past year, and is far more profitable. Workday's edge on the business is its three-year growth record, and that is close to a tie: revenue growth averaged 14.8% a year over three years, against 14.4% for Autodesk.
That near-tie matters because Autodesk's recent pace includes a boost from its new transaction model, worth about 1.5 percentage points of fiscal 2027 revenue growth, that the CFO says will not recur in fiscal 2028. The case for Workday improves if flex credits lift subscription growth above its fiscal 2028 target. To test other names this way, our scorecard rates stocks on growth, profitability, stability, resilience and valuation.
Whichever Stock Wins The Comparison, Concentration Still Loses
A comparison sharpens the pick, but owning too much of either name is the same concentrated bet. Concentration tends to arrive by accident rather than by decision. Workday Named a Leader in Inaugural 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Workforce Management Technology
Workday Unifies Workforce Management, HR, and Payroll on One AI Platform for Smarter Frontline Work
PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Workday, Inc. (NASDAQ: WDAY), the enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT, has been named a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant™ for Workforce Management Technology. A complimentary copy of the report is available here.
Frontline work happens on the floor, in the warehouse, and behind the counter, not in a back office. Workday's workforce management suite brings time tracking, absence management, scheduling, and labor optimization together within Workday Human Capital Management (HCM). This gives frontline leaders one system to manage labor costs, compliance, schedules, and time while giving workers and managers mobile-friendly tools they can use on the go.
"For too long, frontline teams were asked to use technology designed for desk work, not the pace of the floor, the warehouse, or the counter," said David Wachtel, general manager, Workday HCM. "Workday puts that workforce first, with tools that are simple to use and AI that takes the busywork off their plate."
One AI Platform Built for the Way Frontline Teams Work
Workday's workforce management suite is built for the industries where frontline work happens, from retail and manufacturing to hospitality and grocery, and beyond. Capabilities like demand forecasting allow teams to plan ahead and staff to real demand rather than guessing, with AI that reads patterns across seasonality, events, and historical trends to match the right people to the right shifts.
Workday also meets workers where they are, with mobile, web, and kiosk options to clock in. Since schedules, time off, pay, shift swaps, and preferences all live in one place, setting availability or picking up an open shift takes just a few taps.
AI Agents That Give Time Back to Your People
Workday's workforce management suite includes agentic capabilities powered by Sana, Workday's agentic experience, that automates time-consuming tasks, freeing managers and workers to trade desk time for face time.
The Workforce Management Agent automates schedule changes, time tracking, shift swaps, and demand-based staffing, and applies Workday policies, knowledge, and organizational data to optimize scheduling decisions and route approvals according to its configured rules. For example, Workday customers using the Workforce Management Agent in early adoption saw up to a 90% reduction in the time spent managing shift schedule changes, a 65% improvement in process automation on average, and a 75% reduction in manual time entry errors.
With Workday's workforce management suite, automotive services retailer Valvoline cut the time its managers spend generating weekly schedules from more than two hours to about 15 minutes, freeing them to focus on coaching and customers instead of paperwork.
Health and fitness company Life Time hit 95% mobile app adoption after rolling out Workday Scheduling, handing workers real self-service control over their schedules and time. Life Time's managers saved over 50,000 hours each year, and Life Time realized $1 million in annual labor savings and a 50% reduction in overtime costs.

Wall Street is always looking for the next guru. But market history is filled with investors who scored big once, or even a few times, and then faded from history because they didn't keep hitting home runs. That's important to keep in mind as you consider the big shift toward electric stocks in Peter Thiel's portfolio.
Peter Thiel is a famous investor thanks to his successful investments in the technology sector, including Facebook (now called Meta (META +0.30%)). He also helped found PayPal (PYPL -0.49%) and Palantir (PLTR -0.68%). There's a good reason to listen to Thiel when it comes to investing, particularly in the technology sector.
Image source: Getty Images.
However, you don't want to forget that even good investors make mistakes. Warren Buffett, the longtime CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.41%)(BRKB +0.43%) was famous for pointing out his missteps even though his investment approach had been incredibly successful over the long term. Simply put, just because an investor is famous, it doesn't mean you should blindly follow them. They are human, just like you.
What Peter Thiel's shift into energy tells you is that you may want to consider following him... after you do your own homework. As your parents probably asked when you were a kid, "If your friend jumped off a cliff, would you jump too?" When it comes to investing, too many people follow without thinking. You don't want to be one of them.
Is energy the next big thing?
In this situation, Peter Thiel might be on to something. Electricity demand grew 10% between 2005 and 2025, but is expected to climb 60% between 2025 and 2045. That's a step change in demand driven by new technologies like artificial intelligence and electric vehicles. Thiel clearly knows a thing or two about technology and how the industry operates, so a deep dive into electric stocks is probably a good idea.
On that front, Thiel's purchases included independent power producers American Electric Power (AEP -0.15%) and Vistra (VST +0.19%). It also included utility CMS Energy (CMS +0.16%) and nuclear power start-up X-Energy (XE +3.08%). There's a lot going on in that mix, and it might be hard for investors with jobs and lives outside the stock market to dig into and understand all the companies Thiel has chosen to own.
How should you follow Thiel?
If you step back, however, Thiel's broad focus on electricity suggests you could pick just about any electricity-related stock for your portfolio. But you could also select a diversified exchange-traded fund (ETF), such as Vanguard Utilities ETF (VPU +0.43%), which would allow you to follow the electricity theme without taking on stock-specific risk. And if you don't have the time or energy to dig deeply into Thiel's specific stock picks, that may be the better way to play the power theme he appears to be leaning into.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Internet commerce giant PayPal PYPL$52.78·Market Closed extended its blockchain-based stablecoin effort to include a custom stablecoin developer platform, dubbed PYUSDx, built with the help of fiat-pegged token specialist M0 and crypto payments firm MoonPay, the companies said on Tuesday.
The platform, which gives any business the infrastructure to start a custom stablecoin backed by PayPal USD PYUSD$0.9996, was first teased back in February.
It’s now going live with tokens issued by crypto native firms Saturn, Concrete and Cap; which bring over $100 million of processed volume to the platform, according to a press release.
As the existing financial world comes onchain, competition is growing beyond the two major stablecoin issuers: Tether and Circle Internet (CRCL). Established payments companies are searching for a strategic advantage, particularly given the aggressive approach taken by payments giant Stripe, for instance.
PayPal, which CoinDesk revealed was the first payments institution to start offering crypto back in 2020, finds itself at a crossroads, where the sensible move is to partner with crypto specialists like M0 and Moonpay and double down on the tech.
PayPal has already been pushing hard with its PYUSD stablecoin, and the firm is in a unique position to bring this mainstream, considering the enormous reach of Venmo, said Luca Prosperi, CEO of M0, which also works with Stripe-owned Bridge and regulated custody firm Anchorage.
“As more financial institutions are getting involved, this creates fragmentation,” Prosperi said in an interview. “Plus, most of these financial institutions don’t really know how to engage with developers, so we abstract away the complexity and the risk and create a layer in the middle that facilitates integrations with all these new projects.”
PYUSDx tokens are issued by MoonPay Digital Assets Ltd. The platform combines M0’s universal stablecoin and digital token technology with MoonPay’s issuance and distribution infrastructure. Additional companies introducing stablecoins on PYUSDx include USD.AI and Fairblock, according to the release.

What Does PayPal Add to Meta’s Muse?
PayPal has joined Meta’s expanding payments network for Muse, giving users of the personal AI agent another way to complete purchases while extending PayPal’s merchant network into agent-driven shopping.
The integration allows PayPal customers to use Muse to shop and complete purchases at participating PayPal merchants. For Meta, the deal adds another established checkout option as it builds commerce directly into an AI agent that can search for products, interact with websites and act on a user’s instructions.
Muse launched on September 8 and differs from a conventional chatbot because it can perform tasks rather than simply provide answers. The agent can book travel, complete forms and make purchases, including continuing longer tasks in the background while requesting user approval before sensitive actions.
That ability already made payments a central part of Meta’s Muse launch. Adding PayPal now expands the number of merchants and payment credentials that can sit behind those agent-driven transactions.
How Does Muse Complete Purchases?
Meta launched Muse with Stripe’s Link wallet, allowing U.S. consumers to connect saved payment methods and authorize purchases through the agent. Link can complete checkout directly at more than one million businesses that support the service and can generate a single-use virtual card for approved purchases elsewhere.
PayPal gives Muse access to another large payment ecosystem rather than requiring the agent to rely on a single checkout infrastructure. Meta has also integrated Shopify’s Shop Pay and opened Muse to Shopify’s merchant catalog, creating multiple routes through which the agent can move from product discovery to payment.
The model is increasingly important because the competition in AI shopping is moving beyond which assistant can recommend the right product. The harder problem is whether that assistant can actually complete the transaction across enough merchants, payment methods and websites to become useful.
PayPal has already been building toward that model. Its earlier agreement to bring PayPal checkout into ChatGPT connected its merchant network to another AI shopping interface, showing that the company is pursuing distribution across multiple agent platforms rather than betting on one ecosystem.
The strategic value for PayPal is not simply another checkout integration. If consumers increasingly ask AI agents to find products and complete purchases, payment companies will compete to become the infrastructure those agents use automatically. Merchant reach, stored credentials and trusted authorization could become more important than owning the shopping interface itself.
Why Is PayPal Preparing Merchants for AI Agents?
The Muse deal follows PayPal’s September support for WebMCP, an emerging standard designed to make existing merchant websites easier for AI assistants to understand and interact with.
For participating PayPal merchants, WebMCP can expose structured information about products, inventory, carts and checkout to compatible agents without requiring merchants to build a separate AI storefront. The consumer can still approve the payment through PayPal while the agent handles more of the discovery and navigation process.
That matters if agentic commerce develops through the existing web rather than through a handful of closed AI marketplaces. PayPal can potentially make merchants already using its infrastructure accessible to new AI shopping interfaces without forcing those businesses to rebuild their checkout systems.
The payments industry is moving in the same direction. Visa has been developing infrastructure for AI agents to initiate transactions under predefined controls, while a live European test involving Worldline, ING and Visa has already shown that agent-driven purchases can operate within existing banking and authentication rules.
Who Controls the Checkout in Agentic Commerce?
The emerging competition is creating several layers. Meta, OpenAI and other AI companies can control the consumer interface. Shopify and other commerce platforms can provide merchant catalogs. PayPal, Stripe and card networks can provide payment credentials, authorization and settlement.

No single company necessarily needs to control every layer. For PayPal, that could be an advantage. Its business can benefit whenever an agent sends a customer to a PayPal-supported merchant or uses PayPal to complete the transaction, even if another company owns the AI assistant itself.
The challenge is that the same logic attracts competitors. Stripe’s Link already gives Muse broad checkout coverage, while Shop Pay creates another direct route into Shopify stores. Amazon has taken a different approach by blocking Muse from shopping on its platform, showing that merchant access cannot be assumed.
That makes coverage the immediate battleground. An AI shopping agent becomes more useful as the number of websites, catalogs and payment systems it can transact with increases. By adding PayPal, Meta is expanding that reach, while PayPal is making sure its merchant network remains part of the transaction if shopping begins moving from browser tabs to AI agents.

PayPal (PYPL) stock jumped 5% on takeover rumors and a Meta buyout pitch, while Deutsche Bank raised its price target to $55.
By Trader EdgeSeptember 26, 20263 Mins Read
PayPal (PYPL) stock rose about 5% on Friday to $55.13.
Traders cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert pointing to a possible all-stock takeover bid from a West Coast tech company.
PayPal’s board reportedly wants an all-cash deal, not stock.
The Stripe-Advent consortium walked away last month after a dispute over a $2 billion break fee, ending a bid worth over $50 billion.
Deutsche Bank raised its price target on PYPL to $55 from $50, keeping a Hold rating.
PayPal (PYPL) stock climbed roughly 5% on Friday, trading at $55.13 as takeover chatter swirled around the fintech company.
Traders pointed to a Betaville “uncooked” alert circulating Friday morning. The alert suggested a U.S. technology company based on the West Coast could be weighing an all-stock takeover of PayPal.
That’s a different structure than what PayPal’s board reportedly wants. Sources say the board prefers an all-cash transaction over a stock swap.
This isn’t the first takeover talk PayPal has faced this year. Stripe and private equity firm Advent had been in discussions to buy the company outright.
Those talks reportedly hit a snag over a $2 billion break fee. If the deal collapsed, someone would have owed that fee, and neither side could agree on terms.
The Stripe-Advent consortium had considered paying up to $68 per share in cash. That would have valued PayPal at more than $50 billion.
Last month, the consortium reportedly abandoned the pursuit entirely. PayPal has been searching for a suitor since.
PayPal did not respond to requests for comment on the latest speculation, according to Benzinga.
Separately, Great Hill Capital Chairman Thomas Hayes floated his own idea this week. He suggested Meta Platforms (META) should be the one to buy PayPal.
Hayes pitched a price tag of $90 billion. He said that works out to roughly a 7% free-cash-flow yield, calling it accretive whether Meta paid in cash, stock, or some mix of both.
His reasoning centers on data. Hayes argued that pairing PayPal’s transaction data with Meta’s ad business could build advertising capabilities on par with Amazon (AMZN).
He estimated a three-to-four-year payback window on that $90 billion price. Hayes framed the idea as him thinking out loud as a shareholder, not as insider knowledge of any deal.
PYPL is trading about 3% above its 20-day moving average of $53.45. It’s still about 3% below its 50-day average of $56.79, putting the stock in what chart watchers call a decision zone.
The longer-term picture looks steadier. Shares sit roughly 8% above the 100-day average and 9% above the 200-day average.
Relative strength index (RSI) reads 50.75. That’s neutral, not overbought or oversold.
The moving averages tell a mixed story. The 20-day average is still below the 50-day average, a bearish short-term signal.
But the 50-day average remains above the 200-day average following August’s golden cross. That’s typically viewed as a longer-term bullish setup.
Traders are watching whether PYPL can reclaim the 50-day level and hold it. Doing so would turn Friday’s bounce into something more durable.
Key resistance sits at $59.50, a ceiling tied to a recent stall zone. Key support sits at $52, near where the 20-day and 200-day averages converge.
Separately, Deutsche Bank raised its price target on PayPal to $55 from $50 on Friday. The bank kept its Hold rating unchanged.
PayPal shares were up 4.80% to $55.13 at the time of publication Friday.

The payments industry is full of lucrative businesses. Just look at Visa, Mastercard, and American Express. But relative newcomer PayPal (PYPL -0.49%) has struggled mightily in recent years, despite past success. And its investor base has paid the price.
This fintech stock trades at a gut-wrenching 83% off its record high of $305.13 (as of Sept. 29), set in July 2021. Are shares too cheap to ignore right now? Prospective investors will understand that there's only one thing that would send the stock price back to its previous all-time high.
Image source: PayPal.
Branded checkout needs to thrive once again
From the second quarter of 2021 to the most recent quarter (Q2 2026 ended June 30), PayPal's total payment volume (TPV) rose 56%. This helped drive revenue 40% higher during that time. What's more, the company's free cash flow grew by 64%.
While not Earth-shattering growth rates, these are still encouraging financial trends. But despite the fundamental momentum, PayPal's shares have wildly disappointed investors.
I think the culprit is the company's branded checkout solution, which displays the PayPal button for consumers to use when making purchases. This is the company's crown jewel segment, as it's been the most lucrative in the past. In the first and second quarters, TPV here was up just 2%.
This might signal that the PayPal brand is losing its sway among merchants and consumers. Competitive forces are intense these days. Apple Pay is perhaps the most obvious threat, leveraging its advantage of being embedded in the most popular hardware devices.
Furthermore, PayPal's weakness in branded checkout could suggest that its user base is more economically sensitive. Because the platform leans toward discretionary spending activity, the current macroeconomic backdrop could be a headwind as these consumers pull back.

How patient are you willing to be?
For the stock to have a chance at reclaiming its record high, the branded checkout solution has to start picking up steam. This isn't guaranteed, of course. And given trends over recent years, investors are losing confidence.
But if you're still bullish on the business, the cheap price-to-earnings ratio of 10.2 makes this a value stock candidate. And for what it's worth, PayPal remains firmly profitable. It's using FCF to repurchase shares aggressively. This could provide a floor for the stock price, although investor patience will be tested. Shares have been beaten down for a while.
PayPal investors could earn a quick profit if a suitor acquires the business. In July, PayPal rejected a $53 billion takeover bid (priced at $60.50 per share, still well below the all-time record) from Stripe and Advent International, so the board certainly signaled that it wants a much higher offer. Sound investing, however, isn't predicated on guessing when a takeover will happen.
This company has built a scaled global platform and pioneered digital payments for over two decades. But PayPal stock faces a challenging road ahead. I wouldn't bet on it rising 466% to get back to its peak price.

PayPal Survey Reveals Holiday Spending Isn't Slowing Down, But Shoppers Are Changing How They Spend
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 5:32 AM PDT 5 min read
As shoppers start earlier, seek more value and prioritize flexibility, PayPal offers more ways to help them make the most of their holiday budgets.
SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Holiday shoppers aren't necessarily spending less this year. They're changing how they spend. PayPal today released its 2026 Holiday Shopping Survey, revealing that nearly six in 10 Americans (58%) feel greater financial concern heading into the holidays, yet 64% still expect to spend the same or more than they did last holiday season. Faced with that tension, shoppers are planning earlier, setting budgets and looking for more ways to get value from every purchase.
Heading into the holidays, 58% of consumers feel greater financial concern, yet 64% still expect to spend the same or more than last year.
More than half (58%) plan to shop before Thanksgiving, while 67% are more likely to shop with a retailer that offers rewards or cash back. As consumers rethink how they manage holiday spending, PayPal offers more choice and flexibility through Pay Later options, rewarding ways to pay, and offers from top brands in the new PayPal app.
"What's changing isn't consumers' desire to spend during the holidays, but how they're going about it," said Frank Keller, President of Checkout Solutions & PayPal. "Shoppers are starting earlier and taking a more intentional approach, looking for deals, rewards and cash back to make every purchase count while still prioritizing the gifts and moments that matter most. As they look for ways to stretch their budgets, PayPal helps them turn that planning into action by bringing together offers, rewards and flexible payment options, including PayPal Pay Later, throughout the holiday season."
Consumers Are Taking Action to Make Holiday Budgets Go Further
With financial concerns top of mind, shoppers are taking practical steps to manage holiday spending and find value from every purchase, including:
Prioritizing budgets: Setting and sticking to a budget (36%) is the top way consumers plan to manage their holiday spending, followed by comparing prices (32%) and waiting for sales or promotions (31%).
Starting earlier: Two in five consumers plan to begin their holiday shopping by the end of October, and 29% plan to start shopping earlier than last year.
Maximizing rewards: More than two-thirds (67%) are willing to use all their saved rewards to help purchase the perfect gift, and 55% have saved rewards they could use for holiday shopping.
In addition to discovering deals from favorite brands in the PayPal app, shoppers can use the PayPal Cashback Mastercard®1 to earn 3% cash back on eligible purchases when they check out with PayPal.
Shoppers Are Making Tradeoffs to Preserve Gift-Giving
As holiday gift-giving remains a priority, consumers are making careful choices about where to cut back as they balance the season with financial pressures and rising costs.
Sacrifices are personal first: Consumers would cut back on dining out (39%) and gifts for themselves (35%) to make room for holiday spending.
Gift lists may be a little shorter: Twenty-nine percent would buy gifts for fewer people, while 34% would spend less on each individual gift.
Trading time for the perfect gift: Seventy percent are willing to visit multiple stores, while 63% would spend hours searching online for the perfect gift.
As shoppers plan their holiday gift list, clothing (52%), toys and games (38%), and beauty, personal care and fragrance (32%) are the top categories where they plan to buy this holiday season. For larger purchases or gifts for multiple people, flexible payment options from PayPal provide shoppers with another way to manage when and how they pay while keeping meaningful gift-giving within reach.
BNPL Has Become a Go-To Way to Manage Holiday Purchases
The survey also points to strong interest in flexible payment options such as Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), as shoppers consider how to manage the timing and cost of planned holiday expenses. PayPal helps meet that need with Pay Later options including Pay in 42, which allows shoppers to split eligible purchases into four interest-free payments, and Pay Monthly3, which offers longer-term monthly payment plans. The survey found:
BNPL is a core part of the holiday payment mix: More than half of consumers (55%) have used or considered BNPL. Among those consumers, three-quarters plan to use or are considering using BNPL for holiday shopping.
Flexibility and control drive interest: Feeling more in control of their holiday budget and spreading the cost of purchases over time are each valued as BNPL benefits by 59% of consumers, while the flexibility to choose when and how to pay and the ability to take advantage of promotions are each valued by 60%.
BNPL can influence purchase decisions: Forty-two percent say they would be more likely to make a purchase if BNPL were available, 56% value BNPL's ability to help them manage the cost of a higher-value gift, and 57% say it would help them manage the cost of gifts for several people.
PayPal commissioned Morning Consult to survey a nationally representative sample of 2,005 U.S. adults from Sept. 2-4, 2026. The results have a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percentage points.

What Could Derail PayPal Stock?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 12:16 PM PDT 4 min read
PayPal (PYPL) stock has lost 24% in the twelve months to September 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 14.4%. Investors are worried, and you need to know if that worry is overdone. PayPal needs its faster-growing businesses, such as Venmo, to earn more. PayPal also needs shoppers to keep choosing it at online checkout, where trouble could start. So what could go wrong for PayPal at online checkout?
PayPal could lose ground at checkout to competing ways to pay. The business at risk is online branded checkout, the PayPal button on a store's pay page. Management acknowledged the issue on the fiscal Q2 2026 call. Asked about markets outside the U.S., it said there is more competitive intensity across the landscape. Even so, management said PayPal's own performance improved slightly in Europe and was stable in the U.S.
So far, PayPal is holding its place. Online branded checkout volume grew 2% excluding currency moves, the same pace as the quarter before. That pace is slow next to PayPal as a whole. Total payment volume grew 9% in the same quarter, also excluding currency moves. So most of PayPal's volume growth is coming from outside branded checkout.
Is PayPal's Profit Growing As Fast As Its Payments?
No. Transaction margin is the profit PayPal makes on payments before its other operating costs. That profit grew 1% in fiscal Q2 2026, against 9% for payment volume excluding currency moves. Venmo and Braintree, two of PayPal's faster-growing businesses, grew volume in the mid-teens, yet PayPal's total profit on payments barely moved.
PayPal is also keeping a smaller cut of each payment. The take rate is the transaction revenue PayPal earns per dollar of payments. PayPal's take rate fell 7 basis points, or hundredths of a percentage point, to 1.61%. Management said the causes included co-marketing spending on branded checkout and faster growth at Venmo. So PayPal is already spending on marketing for its checkout button.
PayPal reports its whole business as one segment, so branded checkout has no revenue figure of its own. The company as a whole had revenue of $33.2 billion in fiscal 2025. Revenue grew 4.3% that year, down from 6.8% the year before.
The stock costs 9.4 times PayPal's yearly earnings, against 21.7 for the S&P 500. At that price, slow growth appears to be expected. Falling profit would be worse than slow growth, so holders of PayPal stock should watch for signs of it.
What Should You Watch In PayPal's Fiscal Q3 Report?
You should watch branded checkout growth and transaction margin growth in PayPal's fiscal Q3 2026 report. Checkout competition is a real threat to PayPal, but so far a slow one. Branded checkout is still growing, and management raised its full-year outlook for it to low single-digit volume growth.
Because PayPal reports its business as one segment, you cannot tell how much profit branded checkout brings in. So you cannot size the damage if checkout volume starts to shrink. The stock costs 9.4 times today's earnings. If those earnings fall, you are paying more for each dollar of profit than that number shows.
Management guided fiscal Q3 2026 transaction margin to slightly positive growth. PayPal's profit on payments would be shrinking if that number comes in negative. Management also called the holiday quarter always competitive.
PayPal is holding its place at checkout with 2% growth, but its profit on payments is barely growing. Transaction margin growth well above the guide would suggest PayPal's faster-growing businesses, such as Venmo and Braintree, are paying off. Branded checkout growth below 2% in the fiscal Q3 2026 report would be an early warning for PayPal stock.

Wall Street is always looking for the next guru. But market history is filled with investors who scored big once, or even a few times, and then faded from history because they didn't keep hitting home runs. That's important to keep in mind as you consider the big shift toward electric stocks in Peter Thiel's portfolio.
Peter Thiel is a famous investor thanks to his successful investments in the technology sector, including Facebook (now called Meta (META +0.30%)). He also helped found PayPal (PYPL -0.49%) and Palantir (PLTR -0.68%). There's a good reason to listen to Thiel when it comes to investing, particularly in the technology sector.
Image source: Getty Images.
However, you don't want to forget that even good investors make mistakes. Warren Buffett, the longtime CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.41%)(BRKB +0.43%) was famous for pointing out his missteps even though his investment approach had been incredibly successful over the long term. Simply put, just because an investor is famous, it doesn't mean you should blindly follow them. They are human, just like you.
What Peter Thiel's shift into energy tells you is that you may want to consider following him... after you do your own homework. As your parents probably asked when you were a kid, "If your friend jumped off a cliff, would you jump too?" When it comes to investing, too many people follow without thinking. You don't want to be one of them.
Is energy the next big thing?
In this situation, Peter Thiel might be on to something. Electricity demand grew 10% between 2005 and 2025, but is expected to climb 60% between 2025 and 2045. That's a step change in demand driven by new technologies like artificial intelligence and electric vehicles. Thiel clearly knows a thing or two about technology and how the industry operates, so a deep dive into electric stocks is probably a good idea.
On that front, Thiel's purchases included independent power producers American Electric Power (AEP -0.15%) and Vistra (VST +0.19%). It also included utility CMS Energy (CMS +0.16%) and nuclear power start-up X-Energy (XE +3.08%). There's a lot going on in that mix, and it might be hard for investors with jobs and lives outside the stock market to dig into and understand all the companies Thiel has chosen to own.
How should you follow Thiel?
If you step back, however, Thiel's broad focus on electricity suggests you could pick just about any electricity-related stock for your portfolio. But you could also select a diversified exchange-traded fund (ETF), such as Vanguard Utilities ETF (VPU +0.43%), which would allow you to follow the electricity theme without taking on stock-specific risk. And if you don't have the time or energy to dig deeply into Thiel's specific stock picks, that may be the better way to play the power theme he appears to be leaning into.
