Here is What to Know Beyond Why PayPal Holdings, Inc. (PYPL) is a Trending Stock
Paypal (PYPL) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.
Shares of this technology platform and digital payments company have returned -6.6% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.6% change. The Zacks Financial Transaction Services industry, to which Paypal belongs, has lost 4.9% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?
While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.
Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.
We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, Paypal is expected to post earnings of $1.32 per share, indicating a change of -1.5% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0% over the last 30 days.
The consensus earnings estimate of $5.38 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +1.3%. This estimate has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.
For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.8 indicates a change of +7.8% from what Paypal is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.
With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Paypal.
The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:
12-month consensus EPS estimate for PYPL
Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.
In the case of Paypal, the consensus sales estimate of $8.7 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +3.4%. The $34.66 billion and $36.1 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +4.5% and +4.1%, respectively.
Last Reported Results and Surprise History
Paypal reported revenues of $8.68 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +4.8%. EPS of $1.38 for the same period compares with $1.4 a year ago.
Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $8.51 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +2.02%. The EPS surprise was +7.81%.
Over the last four quarters, Paypal surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.
Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.
While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.
As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.
Paypal is graded A on this front, indicating that it is trading at a discount to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.
The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Paypal. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

PayPal expands stablecoin rails with custom token issuance platform
The PYUSDx stablecoin developer platform, backed by PayPal USD (PYUSD), is built with the help of M0 and MoonPay.
PYUSDx goes live with tokens issued by crypto native firms Saturn, Concrete and Cap.
The three go-live partners bring over $100 million of processed volume to the new platform.
Internet commerce giant PayPal PYPL$52.78·Market Closed extended its blockchain-based stablecoin effort to include a custom stablecoin developer platform, dubbed PYUSDx, built with the help of fiat-pegged token specialist M0 and crypto payments firm MoonPay, the companies said on Tuesday.
The platform, which gives any business the infrastructure to start a custom stablecoin backed by PayPal USD PYUSD$0.9996, was first teased back in February.
It’s now going live with tokens issued by crypto native firms Saturn, Concrete and Cap; which bring over $100 million of processed volume to the platform, according to a press release.
As the existing financial world comes onchain, competition is growing beyond the two major stablecoin issuers: Tether and Circle Internet (CRCL). Established payments companies are searching for a strategic advantage, particularly given the aggressive approach taken by payments giant Stripe, for instance.
PayPal, which CoinDesk revealed was the first payments institution to start offering crypto back in 2020, finds itself at a crossroads, where the sensible move is to partner with crypto specialists like M0 and Moonpay and double down on the tech.
PayPal has already been pushing hard with its PYUSD stablecoin, and the firm is in a unique position to bring this mainstream, considering the enormous reach of Venmo, said Luca Prosperi, CEO of M0, which also works with Stripe-owned Bridge and regulated custody firm Anchorage.
“As more financial institutions are getting involved, this creates fragmentation,” Prosperi said in an interview. “Plus, most of these financial institutions don’t really know how to engage with developers, so we abstract away the complexity and the risk and create a layer in the middle that facilitates integrations with all these new projects.”
PYUSDx tokens are issued by MoonPay Digital Assets Ltd. The platform combines M0’s universal stablecoin and digital token technology with MoonPay’s issuance and distribution infrastructure. Additional companies introducing stablecoins on PYUSDx include USD.AI and Fairblock, according to the release.

PayPal Customers Can Now Shop Through Meta’s Muse AI Agent
What Does PayPal Add to Meta’s Muse?
PayPal has joined Meta’s expanding payments network for Muse, giving users of the personal AI agent another way to complete purchases while extending PayPal’s merchant network into agent-driven shopping.
The integration allows PayPal customers to use Muse to shop and complete purchases at participating PayPal merchants. For Meta, the deal adds another established checkout option as it builds commerce directly into an AI agent that can search for products, interact with websites and act on a user’s instructions.
Muse launched on September 8 and differs from a conventional chatbot because it can perform tasks rather than simply provide answers. The agent can book travel, complete forms and make purchases, including continuing longer tasks in the background while requesting user approval before sensitive actions.
That ability already made payments a central part of Meta’s Muse launch. Adding PayPal now expands the number of merchants and payment credentials that can sit behind those agent-driven transactions.
How Does Muse Complete Purchases?
Meta launched Muse with Stripe’s Link wallet, allowing U.S. consumers to connect saved payment methods and authorize purchases through the agent. Link can complete checkout directly at more than one million businesses that support the service and can generate a single-use virtual card for approved purchases elsewhere.
PayPal gives Muse access to another large payment ecosystem rather than requiring the agent to rely on a single checkout infrastructure. Meta has also integrated Shopify’s Shop Pay and opened Muse to Shopify’s merchant catalog, creating multiple routes through which the agent can move from product discovery to payment.
The model is increasingly important because the competition in AI shopping is moving beyond which assistant can recommend the right product. The harder problem is whether that assistant can actually complete the transaction across enough merchants, payment methods and websites to become useful.
PayPal has already been building toward that model. Its earlier agreement to bring PayPal checkout into ChatGPT connected its merchant network to another AI shopping interface, showing that the company is pursuing distribution across multiple agent platforms rather than betting on one ecosystem.
The strategic value for PayPal is not simply another checkout integration. If consumers increasingly ask AI agents to find products and complete purchases, payment companies will compete to become the infrastructure those agents use automatically. Merchant reach, stored credentials and trusted authorization could become more important than owning the shopping interface itself.
Why Is PayPal Preparing Merchants for AI Agents?
The Muse deal follows PayPal’s September support for WebMCP, an emerging standard designed to make existing merchant websites easier for AI assistants to understand and interact with.
For participating PayPal merchants, WebMCP can expose structured information about products, inventory, carts and checkout to compatible agents without requiring merchants to build a separate AI storefront. The consumer can still approve the payment through PayPal while the agent handles more of the discovery and navigation process.
That matters if agentic commerce develops through the existing web rather than through a handful of closed AI marketplaces. PayPal can potentially make merchants already using its infrastructure accessible to new AI shopping interfaces without forcing those businesses to rebuild their checkout systems.
The payments industry is moving in the same direction. Visa has been developing infrastructure for AI agents to initiate transactions under predefined controls, while a live European test involving Worldline, ING and Visa has already shown that agent-driven purchases can operate within existing banking and authentication rules.
Who Controls the Checkout in Agentic Commerce?
The emerging competition is creating several layers. Meta, OpenAI and other AI companies can control the consumer interface. Shopify and other commerce platforms can provide merchant catalogs. PayPal, Stripe and card networks can provide payment credentials, authorization and settlement.
RelatedPayPal Q2 2026: $1.38 EPS Beat, But Operating Income Fell 8%
No single company necessarily needs to control every layer. For PayPal, that could be an advantage. Its business can benefit whenever an agent sends a customer to a PayPal-supported merchant or uses PayPal to complete the transaction, even if another company owns the AI assistant itself.
The challenge is that the same logic attracts competitors. Stripe’s Link already gives Muse broad checkout coverage, while Shop Pay creates another direct route into Shopify stores. Amazon has taken a different approach by blocking Muse from shopping on its platform, showing that merchant access cannot be assumed.
That makes coverage the immediate battleground. An AI shopping agent becomes more useful as the number of websites, catalogs and payment systems it can transact with increases. By adding PayPal, Meta is expanding that reach, while PayPal is making sure its merchant network remains part of the transaction if shopping begins moving from browser tabs to AI agents.

PayPal (PYPL) Stock Jumps 5% on Takeover Buzz and Meta Deal Chatter
PayPal (PYPL) stock jumped 5% on takeover rumors and a Meta buyout pitch, while Deutsche Bank raised its price target to $55.
By Trader EdgeSeptember 26, 20263 Mins Read
PayPal (PYPL) stock rose about 5% on Friday to $55.13.
Traders cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert pointing to a possible all-stock takeover bid from a West Coast tech company.
PayPal’s board reportedly wants an all-cash deal, not stock.
The Stripe-Advent consortium walked away last month after a dispute over a $2 billion break fee, ending a bid worth over $50 billion.
Deutsche Bank raised its price target on PYPL to $55 from $50, keeping a Hold rating.
PayPal (PYPL) stock climbed roughly 5% on Friday, trading at $55.13 as takeover chatter swirled around the fintech company.
Traders pointed to a Betaville “uncooked” alert circulating Friday morning. The alert suggested a U.S. technology company based on the West Coast could be weighing an all-stock takeover of PayPal.
That’s a different structure than what PayPal’s board reportedly wants. Sources say the board prefers an all-cash transaction over a stock swap.
This isn’t the first takeover talk PayPal has faced this year. Stripe and private equity firm Advent had been in discussions to buy the company outright.
Those talks reportedly hit a snag over a $2 billion break fee. If the deal collapsed, someone would have owed that fee, and neither side could agree on terms.
The Stripe-Advent consortium had considered paying up to $68 per share in cash. That would have valued PayPal at more than $50 billion.
Last month, the consortium reportedly abandoned the pursuit entirely. PayPal has been searching for a suitor since.
PayPal did not respond to requests for comment on the latest speculation, according to Benzinga.
Separately, Great Hill Capital Chairman Thomas Hayes floated his own idea this week. He suggested Meta Platforms (META) should be the one to buy PayPal.
Hayes pitched a price tag of $90 billion. He said that works out to roughly a 7% free-cash-flow yield, calling it accretive whether Meta paid in cash, stock, or some mix of both.
His reasoning centers on data. Hayes argued that pairing PayPal’s transaction data with Meta’s ad business could build advertising capabilities on par with Amazon (AMZN).
He estimated a three-to-four-year payback window on that $90 billion price. Hayes framed the idea as him thinking out loud as a shareholder, not as insider knowledge of any deal.
PYPL is trading about 3% above its 20-day moving average of $53.45. It’s still about 3% below its 50-day average of $56.79, putting the stock in what chart watchers call a decision zone.
The longer-term picture looks steadier. Shares sit roughly 8% above the 100-day average and 9% above the 200-day average.
Relative strength index (RSI) reads 50.75. That’s neutral, not overbought or oversold.
The moving averages tell a mixed story. The 20-day average is still below the 50-day average, a bearish short-term signal.
But the 50-day average remains above the 200-day average following August’s golden cross. That’s typically viewed as a longer-term bullish setup.
Traders are watching whether PYPL can reclaim the 50-day level and hold it. Doing so would turn Friday’s bounce into something more durable.
Key resistance sits at $59.50, a ceiling tied to a recent stall zone. Key support sits at $52, near where the 20-day and 200-day averages converge.
Separately, Deutsche Bank raised its price target on PayPal to $55 from $50 on Friday. The bank kept its Hold rating unchanged.
PayPal shares were up 4.80% to $55.13 at the time of publication Friday.

The payments industry is full of lucrative businesses. Just look at Visa, Mastercard, and American Express. But relative newcomer PayPal (PYPL -0.49%) has struggled mightily in recent years, despite past success. And its investor base has paid the price.
This fintech stock trades at a gut-wrenching 83% off its record high of $305.13 (as of Sept. 29), set in July 2021. Are shares too cheap to ignore right now? Prospective investors will understand that there's only one thing that would send the stock price back to its previous all-time high.
Image source: PayPal.
Branded checkout needs to thrive once again
From the second quarter of 2021 to the most recent quarter (Q2 2026 ended June 30), PayPal's total payment volume (TPV) rose 56%. This helped drive revenue 40% higher during that time. What's more, the company's free cash flow grew by 64%.
While not Earth-shattering growth rates, these are still encouraging financial trends. But despite the fundamental momentum, PayPal's shares have wildly disappointed investors.
I think the culprit is the company's branded checkout solution, which displays the PayPal button for consumers to use when making purchases. This is the company's crown jewel segment, as it's been the most lucrative in the past. In the first and second quarters, TPV here was up just 2%.
This might signal that the PayPal brand is losing its sway among merchants and consumers. Competitive forces are intense these days. Apple Pay is perhaps the most obvious threat, leveraging its advantage of being embedded in the most popular hardware devices.
Furthermore, PayPal's weakness in branded checkout could suggest that its user base is more economically sensitive. Because the platform leans toward discretionary spending activity, the current macroeconomic backdrop could be a headwind as these consumers pull back.
$45BMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
How patient are you willing to be?
For the stock to have a chance at reclaiming its record high, the branded checkout solution has to start picking up steam. This isn't guaranteed, of course. And given trends over recent years, investors are losing confidence.
But if you're still bullish on the business, the cheap price-to-earnings ratio of 10.2 makes this a value stock candidate. And for what it's worth, PayPal remains firmly profitable. It's using FCF to repurchase shares aggressively. This could provide a floor for the stock price, although investor patience will be tested. Shares have been beaten down for a while.
PayPal investors could earn a quick profit if a suitor acquires the business. In July, PayPal rejected a $53 billion takeover bid (priced at $60.50 per share, still well below the all-time record) from Stripe and Advent International, so the board certainly signaled that it wants a much higher offer. Sound investing, however, isn't predicated on guessing when a takeover will happen.
This company has built a scaled global platform and pioneered digital payments for over two decades. But PayPal stock faces a challenging road ahead. I wouldn't bet on it rising 466% to get back to its peak price.

PayPal Survey Reveals Holiday Spending Isn't Slowing Down, But Shoppers Are Changing How They Spend
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 5:32 AM PDT 5 min read
As shoppers start earlier, seek more value and prioritize flexibility, PayPal offers more ways to help them make the most of their holiday budgets.
SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Holiday shoppers aren't necessarily spending less this year. They're changing how they spend. PayPal today released its 2026 Holiday Shopping Survey, revealing that nearly six in 10 Americans (58%) feel greater financial concern heading into the holidays, yet 64% still expect to spend the same or more than they did last holiday season. Faced with that tension, shoppers are planning earlier, setting budgets and looking for more ways to get value from every purchase.
Heading into the holidays, 58% of consumers feel greater financial concern, yet 64% still expect to spend the same or more than last year.
More than half (58%) plan to shop before Thanksgiving, while 67% are more likely to shop with a retailer that offers rewards or cash back. As consumers rethink how they manage holiday spending, PayPal offers more choice and flexibility through Pay Later options, rewarding ways to pay, and offers from top brands in the new PayPal app.
"What's changing isn't consumers' desire to spend during the holidays, but how they're going about it," said Frank Keller, President of Checkout Solutions & PayPal. "Shoppers are starting earlier and taking a more intentional approach, looking for deals, rewards and cash back to make every purchase count while still prioritizing the gifts and moments that matter most. As they look for ways to stretch their budgets, PayPal helps them turn that planning into action by bringing together offers, rewards and flexible payment options, including PayPal Pay Later, throughout the holiday season."
Consumers Are Taking Action to Make Holiday Budgets Go Further
With financial concerns top of mind, shoppers are taking practical steps to manage holiday spending and find value from every purchase, including:
Prioritizing budgets: Setting and sticking to a budget (36%) is the top way consumers plan to manage their holiday spending, followed by comparing prices (32%) and waiting for sales or promotions (31%).
Starting earlier: Two in five consumers plan to begin their holiday shopping by the end of October, and 29% plan to start shopping earlier than last year.
Maximizing rewards: More than two-thirds (67%) are willing to use all their saved rewards to help purchase the perfect gift, and 55% have saved rewards they could use for holiday shopping.
In addition to discovering deals from favorite brands in the PayPal app, shoppers can use the PayPal Cashback Mastercard®1 to earn 3% cash back on eligible purchases when they check out with PayPal.
Shoppers Are Making Tradeoffs to Preserve Gift-Giving
As holiday gift-giving remains a priority, consumers are making careful choices about where to cut back as they balance the season with financial pressures and rising costs.
Sacrifices are personal first: Consumers would cut back on dining out (39%) and gifts for themselves (35%) to make room for holiday spending.
Gift lists may be a little shorter: Twenty-nine percent would buy gifts for fewer people, while 34% would spend less on each individual gift.
Trading time for the perfect gift: Seventy percent are willing to visit multiple stores, while 63% would spend hours searching online for the perfect gift.
As shoppers plan their holiday gift list, clothing (52%), toys and games (38%), and beauty, personal care and fragrance (32%) are the top categories where they plan to buy this holiday season. For larger purchases or gifts for multiple people, flexible payment options from PayPal provide shoppers with another way to manage when and how they pay while keeping meaningful gift-giving within reach.
BNPL Has Become a Go-To Way to Manage Holiday Purchases
The survey also points to strong interest in flexible payment options such as Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), as shoppers consider how to manage the timing and cost of planned holiday expenses. PayPal helps meet that need with Pay Later options including Pay in 42, which allows shoppers to split eligible purchases into four interest-free payments, and Pay Monthly3, which offers longer-term monthly payment plans. The survey found:
BNPL is a core part of the holiday payment mix: More than half of consumers (55%) have used or considered BNPL. Among those consumers, three-quarters plan to use or are considering using BNPL for holiday shopping.
Flexibility and control drive interest: Feeling more in control of their holiday budget and spreading the cost of purchases over time are each valued as BNPL benefits by 59% of consumers, while the flexibility to choose when and how to pay and the ability to take advantage of promotions are each valued by 60%.
BNPL can influence purchase decisions: Forty-two percent say they would be more likely to make a purchase if BNPL were available, 56% value BNPL's ability to help them manage the cost of a higher-value gift, and 57% say it would help them manage the cost of gifts for several people.
PayPal commissioned Morning Consult to survey a nationally representative sample of 2,005 U.S. adults from Sept. 2-4, 2026. The results have a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percentage points.

What Could Derail PayPal Stock?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 12:16 PM PDT 4 min read
PayPal (PYPL) stock has lost 24% in the twelve months to September 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 14.4%. Investors are worried, and you need to know if that worry is overdone. PayPal needs its faster-growing businesses, such as Venmo, to earn more. PayPal also needs shoppers to keep choosing it at online checkout, where trouble could start. So what could go wrong for PayPal at online checkout?
PayPal could lose ground at checkout to competing ways to pay. The business at risk is online branded checkout, the PayPal button on a store's pay page. Management acknowledged the issue on the fiscal Q2 2026 call. Asked about markets outside the U.S., it said there is more competitive intensity across the landscape. Even so, management said PayPal's own performance improved slightly in Europe and was stable in the U.S.
So far, PayPal is holding its place. Online branded checkout volume grew 2% excluding currency moves, the same pace as the quarter before. That pace is slow next to PayPal as a whole. Total payment volume grew 9% in the same quarter, also excluding currency moves. So most of PayPal's volume growth is coming from outside branded checkout.
Is PayPal's Profit Growing As Fast As Its Payments?
No. Transaction margin is the profit PayPal makes on payments before its other operating costs. That profit grew 1% in fiscal Q2 2026, against 9% for payment volume excluding currency moves. Venmo and Braintree, two of PayPal's faster-growing businesses, grew volume in the mid-teens, yet PayPal's total profit on payments barely moved.
PayPal is also keeping a smaller cut of each payment. The take rate is the transaction revenue PayPal earns per dollar of payments. PayPal's take rate fell 7 basis points, or hundredths of a percentage point, to 1.61%. Management said the causes included co-marketing spending on branded checkout and faster growth at Venmo. So PayPal is already spending on marketing for its checkout button.
PayPal reports its whole business as one segment, so branded checkout has no revenue figure of its own. The company as a whole had revenue of $33.2 billion in fiscal 2025. Revenue grew 4.3% that year, down from 6.8% the year before.
The stock costs 9.4 times PayPal's yearly earnings, against 21.7 for the S&P 500. At that price, slow growth appears to be expected. Falling profit would be worse than slow growth, so holders of PayPal stock should watch for signs of it.
What Should You Watch In PayPal's Fiscal Q3 Report?
You should watch branded checkout growth and transaction margin growth in PayPal's fiscal Q3 2026 report. Checkout competition is a real threat to PayPal, but so far a slow one. Branded checkout is still growing, and management raised its full-year outlook for it to low single-digit volume growth.
Because PayPal reports its business as one segment, you cannot tell how much profit branded checkout brings in. So you cannot size the damage if checkout volume starts to shrink. The stock costs 9.4 times today's earnings. If those earnings fall, you are paying more for each dollar of profit than that number shows.
Management guided fiscal Q3 2026 transaction margin to slightly positive growth. PayPal's profit on payments would be shrinking if that number comes in negative. Management also called the holiday quarter always competitive.
PayPal is holding its place at checkout with 2% growth, but its profit on payments is barely growing. Transaction margin growth well above the guide would suggest PayPal's faster-growing businesses, such as Venmo and Braintree, are paying off. Branded checkout growth below 2% in the fiscal Q3 2026 report would be an early warning for PayPal stock.

Payments network operator PayPal (PYPL) saw its stock drop sharply after a consortium of buyout firm Advent International and payment processor Stripe walked away from a $53 billion (or $60.50 per share) bid after being rebuffed.
Now, PayPal has been embroiled in rumors of another takeover bid. Traders reported that an "uncooked" alert from Betaville suggested a U.S. technology company headquartered on the West Coast could be considering an all-stock acquisition of the fintech company. Reportedly, PayPal is looking for an all-cash offer. While nothing is confirmed, PayPal might not accept an offer that is not meaningfully above $70 per share, as Bernstein analysts estimate.

Meanwhile, PayPal is looking to turn around from slowing fundamentals under its new CEO, Enrique Lores. To achieve this restructuring, the company has made multiple workforce reductions as a cost-saving measure. Agentic AI also offers a unique growth opportunity for a firm like PayPal, given its existing customer base.
While the takeover bid rumors are not yet conclusive, let's take a look at PayPal's current state.
PayPal Holdings runs a worldwide payments network that connects consumers and businesses across digital and physical channels. Its brands, including PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom, allow users to make purchases, transfer funds, receive payments, and access various financial services.
The company works with consumers, small businesses, global retailers, online marketplaces, and other corporate customers. In addition to processing payments, PayPal offers fraud management, payment authorization, and business analytics solutions designed to help merchants improve transactions and customer engagement. Headquartered in San Jose, California, the company has a market capitalization of approximately $46.43 billion.
PYPL stock has fallen 20% over the past 52 weeks, mainly because investors remain concerned about slowing growth, intense competition, and uncertainty over the company's turnaround. It reached a 52-week low of $38.46 in February but is up 39% from that level. However, the stock rose 24% over the past three months as investors saw signs of improvement. Reports of the potential takeover bid supported the stock by highlighting PayPal's strategic value.
On a forward-adjusted basis, PayPal's price-to-earnings (non-GAAP) ratio of 10.07x is lower than the industry average of 10.96x.
Revenue Growth in Q2 Raises Full-Year Profit Guidance
In the second quarter, PayPal reported 10% year-over-year (YoY) growth in total payment volume to $486.45 billion, while quarterly revenue rose 5% YoY to $8.68 billion. As operating cash flow improved sharply and capital spending remained modest, the company's free cash flow climbed 157% YoY to $1.78 billion. However, PayPal's adjusted operating margin dropped by 248 basis points to 17.4%. Adjusted EPS declined by 1% YoY to $1.38.
PayPal raised its fiscal 2026 non-GAAP EPS forecast to about $5.38, slightly above the $5.31 figure it recorded in fiscal 2025. In its last guidance, the company expected non-GAAP EPS to decline in the low single digits or increase slightly. For the current year, Wall Street analysts expect PayPal's EPS to increase by a modest 1.3% YoY to $5.38, followed by a 7.8% improvement to $5.80 in the next year. However, for the third quarter, EPS is projected to decrease 1.5% YoY to $1.32.
What Do Analysts Think About PYPL Stock?
In August, analysts at Piper Sandler raised the price target on PYPL stock from $42 to $59 while maintaining a "Neutral" rating, following reports that PayPal is negotiating a higher takeover bid from Stripe and Advent. The analyst saw this development as a potential strategic validation of the company's asset base. However, later reports suggested that the group is no longer pursuing the takeover after their initial offer was rebuffed. This led analysts at Truist Securities to lower PayPal's price target from $62 to $53 while keeping a "Hold" rating on its shares.
Contrarily, RBC Capital analysts raised PayPal's price target from $65 to $70 and maintained an "Outperform" rating as part of a broader research note on Fintech & Payments as RBC updates its valuation framework.
Wall Street analysts are taking a cautious stance on PYPL's stock now, with a consensus "Hold" rating overall. Of the 46 analysts rating the stock, four analysts gave a "Strong Buy" rating, and two analysts rated it "Moderate Buy," while a majority of 36 analysts are playing it safe with a "Hold" rating; one analyst suggested "Moderate Sell," and three analysts gave a "Strong Sell" rating. The consensus price target of $56.03 represents a 5% upside from current levels. The Street-high price target of $72 implies a 36% upside.

PayPal (PYPL) Stock Gets Fair Value Trim As Analysts Weigh Q2 And Deal Uncertainty
Analysts have trimmed their central fair value estimate for PayPal Holdings, with the model price target moving from US$59.16 to US$57.07. The revision comes amid mixed research views, with some analysts highlighting Q2 earnings and asset value, while others focus on competition, questions about a takeover, and recent share moves linked to deal headlines. As you read on, you will see how this updated target fits into the broader PayPal narrative and what signals to watch next.
Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value PayPal Holdings.
Several firms lifted PayPal price targets after the Q2 report, citing the earnings beat, higher guidance and signs of stabilisation in Branded Checkout and payment volumes. RBC Capital, Keefe Bruyette, Argus, TD Cowen, UBS and others pushed targets into the US$56 to US$70 range while generally pointing to improving fundamentals and early traction in the turnaround plan.
Some analysts see the recent takeover interest as support for PayPal's asset base. Piper Sandler and BMO highlighted third party interest and a formal bid as validation of assets such as Venmo, global licences and risk infrastructure, with several firms including Cantor Fitzgerald and William Blair indicating that a price nearer US$70 per share would better align with their valuation work.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley remain cautious on PayPal. They keep Sell or Underweight ratings and point to concerns around branded checkout share, limited standalone options for faster growth and what they view as constraints on multiple expansion despite Q2 strength.
More recently, Truist cut its target to US$53 and flagged questions around the strategic logic and pricing of a potential Stripe acquisition. BTIG and BofA also emphasised that near term moves in PayPal stock may be driven more by deal headlines than by ongoing execution of the transformation plan.

MARA stock wasn't chasing this move alone. Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood all rallied the same session, and rival miners moved in step.

MARA Holdings (MARA) shares climbed roughly 5% during Monday’s session, reaching approximately $13.90 as Bitcoin broke through the $85,000 mark. The digital currency hit its strongest level in months, providing a tailwind for cryptocurrency-related equities as the week began.
The primary driver behind Monday’s advance is Bitcoin’s renewed strength. MARA generates the bulk of its revenue through Bitcoin mining operations and maintains Bitcoin holdings on its corporate balance sheet, creating a direct connection between the stock and cryptocurrency price movements.
When Bitcoin prices rise, mining profitability typically improves since operational costs are denominated in fiat currency while mining rewards fluctuate with Bitcoin’s dollar value. This dynamic often amplifies MARA’s stock movements relative to Bitcoin during periods of cryptocurrency strength.
Monday’s advance follows an already positive week for the shares. MARA posted an 8.3% gain Friday as market participants digested fresh analyst commentary and the company’s strategic pivot toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing operations.
Cryptocurrency Strength Powers MARA Advance
Bitcoin’s climb beyond $85,000 capped multiple days of gains and boosted sentiment throughout the cryptocurrency equity sector. Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood also posted advances as capital flowed back into digital-asset stocks.
For MARA, Bitcoin’s price movement carries outsized importance because mining profitability hinges on the market value of each Bitcoin mined. Fixed costs including electricity, equipment depreciation and facility expenses don’t automatically scale with Bitcoin prices.
This creates operational leverage during Bitcoin rallies. Conversely, declining Bitcoin prices can squeeze mining margins and reduce the value of MARA’s cryptocurrency holdings.
MARA has been working to diversify beyond pure Bitcoin mining activities. The company increasingly positions itself as a digital infrastructure and energy enterprise with growing exposure to AI data centers and high-performance computing facilities.

H.C. Wainwright emphasized MARA’s collaboration with Starwood Capital alongside its proposed acquisition of Long Ridge Energy. The analyst suggests these assets could position MARA to secure AI data-center leasing agreements in the years ahead.
Morgan Stanley has adopted a more reserved stance. The firm recently increased its MARA target to $11 from $6 while maintaining a bearish outlook, and J.P. Morgan similarly maintains an $11 price objective.
J.P. Morgan has previously questioned MARA’s execution on its data-center transition and raised concerns about the feasibility of converting certain mining facilities. This divergence highlights Wall Street’s uncertainty regarding the ultimate value creation potential of the AI strategy.
MARA’s sharp rebound also underscores the importance of considering volatility. Despite recent gains, the stock trades well below its 52-week peak, and price swings can accelerate when Bitcoin shifts direction.
The AI strategy also introduces execution challenges since data-center projects demand significant capital investment, appropriate power infrastructure and long-term customer commitments. Any setbacks in asset conversion or tenant acquisition could undermine the valuation thesis.
For Monday’s session, though, the primary catalyst remains Bitcoin’s breakout above $85,000. MARA’s cryptocurrency exposure combined with fresh analyst attention to its AI ambitions delivered another day of gains.

Mara Holdings stock (ISIN US56575P1084) has surged sharply in recent sessions, with the Nasdaq-listed shares breaking above the 12 dollar level on September 18, 2026 amid an analyst price target revision and a broad rally in crypto-related names.
Analyst upgrade and AI pivot fuel the move
According to Investing.com on September 18, 2026, Mara Holdings stock jumped 8.3 percent in morning trading to 12.61 dollars after Morgan Stanley maintained its Underweight rating but nearly doubled its price target to 11 dollars from a prior 6 dollars, signaling a notable reassessment of downside risk in the shares.
As Investing.com reports, the move came as investors increasingly focus on the company’s strategic transformation toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing infrastructure, which is designed to complement its roots in digital asset and crypto mining.
Technically, the 12 dollar level had acted as a resistance zone in prior sessions, and the breach above this threshold on September 18, 2026 triggered further momentum buying and options-related activity, with 12 dollar strike call options expiring that day adding leverage to the move, according to Investing.com.
The price momentum in Mara Holdings stock has been underpinned by a renewed surge in crypto markets. As Sina Finance reports on September 19, 2026, Bitcoin briefly moved back above 80,000 dollars, and crypto-related equities rallied strongly, with Mara Holdings closing up nearly 13.8 percent, outpacing even the underlying move in the leading cryptocurrency.
Against this backdrop of rising prices, multiple insider sales have been disclosed. According to Investing.com on September 19, 2026, Chief Executive Officer Frederick G. Thiel sold 27,505 shares on September 17, 2026 at 11.45 dollars per share for proceeds of 314,932 dollars, and continues to hold 4,308,192 shares after the transaction.
In a separate filing, Mara Holdings Chief Financial Officer Salman Hassan Khan sold 16,000 shares of common stock on September 17, 2026 at 11.45 dollars per share, for a total value of 183,200 dollars, as reported by Investing.com on September 19, 2026.
The insider activity extends to the legal function as well. General Counsel Nowaid Zabi sold 8,376 shares on September 18, 2026 at a weighted average price of 12.10 dollars per share, for total proceeds of 101,349 dollars, and the stock has since risen to around 13.25 dollars, marking a gain of 10.5 percent over the past week and a 44 percent increase over the last six months, according to Investing.com.
Recent Q2 2026 results highlight earnings risk
While the share price has been moving higher, Mara Holdings’ most recent quarterly numbers underscore the volatility of its earnings profile. In its second quarter 2026 results, Marathon Digital Holdings reported a substantial net loss of 611.3 million dollars, compared to a net profit of 808.2 million dollars in the prior-year period, as summarized by Investing.com.
According to the same overview, earnings per share for the second quarter 2026 came in at a loss of 1.60 dollars, missing analyst expectations that had anticipated a profit of 0.35 dollars per share, meaning the reported EPS undershot consensus by 1.95 dollars.
Second quarter 2026 revenue reached 174.9 million dollars but fell short of forecasts of 208.37 million dollars, implying the top line was about 33.47 million dollars below expectations, as highlighted by Investing.com.
For investors, the combination of a sizable quarterly loss and a revenue shortfall against consensus is a reminder that Mara’s pivot toward AI infrastructure and high-performance computing still carries execution and market risk, even as sentiment currently benefits from the crypto rally and revised analyst targets.
Beyond the specific Morgan Stanley revision, aggregate analyst views remain cautious. As MarketBeat reported on September 18, 2026, data from its coverage show Mara currently carrying an average rating of Hold with a consensus price target of around 18.70 dollars, suggesting upside potential from the low teens but also reflecting divided views on the company’s risk profile.
In a subsequent snapshot on September 19, 2026, MarketBeat noted that the consensus rating remained at Hold with an average target around 19.20 dollars, a modest increase that aligns broadly with the Morgan Stanley lift and recent bullish initiation commentary from other houses.
The broader sector move has also supported Mara’s valuation. A US market wrap from Sina Finance on September 19, 2026 highlighted that crypto-related stocks including Mara Holdings gained over 13 percent on the day, outstripping broader indices such as the Nasdaq, which rose 0.39 percent over the same session.
Per recent trading data cited by several Investing.com summaries on September 19, 2026, Mara Holdings stock has recently traded around 13.25 dollars on the Nasdaq, implying a gain of roughly 16 percent from the 11.45 dollar level where CEO Frederick Thiel and CFO Salman Hassan Khan executed their sales on September 17, 2026 and reflecting a 44 percent rise over the past six months.
According to Investing.com, at these levels the company’s market capitalization stands at approximately 4.5 billion dollars, putting Mara firmly in the mid-cap bracket among US-listed technology and digital asset infrastructure firms.
For retail investors, the key takeaway is that Mara Holdings stock now trades in the low teens in USD on Nasdaq as of September 19, 2026, not far above the recently cleared 12 dollar resistance, in a market environment where analyst targets have moved higher but recent fundamentals still reflect elevated earnings volatility.

MARA Stock Rose 14% Friday. JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley Still Don’t Agree.
MARA Stock Rose 14% Friday. JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley Still Don't Agree. ©TIKR
Bitcoin Rebound: MARA stock jumped 14% Friday as bitcoin surged near $81,000.
Split Verdict: Six buys, two outperforms, four holds, one underperform and one sell make up the 14 analysts TIKR tracks on MARA stock, whose mean target of $18 sits 39% above Friday's close.
Wall Street Reframe: Morgan Stanley nearly doubled its target on MARA stock to $11 from $6 while still rating it Underweight, tying the new number to the company's pivot into AI data center power.
Why MARA Stock Jumped 14% on Bitcoin's Friday Rally
MARA Holdings (MARA) stock jumped 14% on Friday, September 18, 2026, closing at $13.24 as bitcoin ripped roughly 6% higher, near $81,000 and pulled the entire crypto mining sector along with it. MARA stock wasn't chasing this move alone. Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood all rallied the same session, and rival miners moved in step.
The rally had a second leg. The same day, Morgan Stanley raised its price target on MARA stock to $11 from $6, nearly doubling the number while keeping its Underweight rating in place. The bank tied the new target to MARA Holdings' shift away from pure Bitcoin mining and into AI data center power, pointing to the Matagorda County project in Texas, planned for up to two gigawatts of capacity, and the $1.5 billion purchase of Ohio's Long Ridge power plant.
That framing landed four days after a very different call. On Monday, September 14, JPMorgan cut MARA stock to Underweight from Overweight and slashed its own target to $11 from $13. So Wall Street enters this rally without agreeing on what the AI pivot actually adds to the stock. Friday's 14% move priced in the crypto rebound. It didn't settle that argument.
MARA Stock's Analyst Split Grows More Combative Since Spring
Six analysts rate MARA stock a buy and two more call it an outperform. Four hold ratings, one underperform and one sell round out the 14 analysts TIKR tracks as of September 18.
Street Analysts Target for MARA Stock (TIKR)
Their mean target sits at $18, 39% above Friday's close of $13.
That gap would have looked unremarkable a year ago. What changed is the shape of the coverage, not just its average. Back in September 2025, the mean target ran to $23 while MARA stock closed near $18. Then the stock cratered, falling past $9 by December and to $8 by March 2026, a decline of more than half its value in six months. The Street barely moved in that first quarter of the drop, cutting its mean target from $23 to just $22. The real cut came later, when the mean fell to $17 as the stock kept sliding toward its low.
Since March, both numbers have climbed back together. MARA stock recovered to $14 by June and sits near $13 now, and the mean target rose to $18, roughly where it stands today. But the coverage itself has grown more contested rather than more settled. September marks the first quarter in this table carrying an underperform rating on MARA stock, arriving through JPMorgan's Monday downgrade just four days before Friday's rally. Even Morgan Stanley's new target keeps an Underweight attached. The bulls at H.C. Wainwright hold a $20 target. The stock just jumped 14%, and the analysts covering it are further apart than they were in the spring.
Should You Invest in MARA Holdings, Inc.?
The only way to really know is to look at the numbers yourself. TIKR gives you free access to the same institutional-quality financial data that professional analysts use to answer exactly that question.
Pull up MARA Holdings, Inc. stock and you'll see years of historical financials, what Wall Street analysts expect for revenue and earnings in the quarters ahead, how valuation multiples have moved over time, and whether price targets are trending up or down.

Booking (BKNG) vs Airbnb (ABNB): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) closed at $159.02 on October 2, and Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) at $162.43.
The two share prices are almost identical. Over the past twelve months, one of them rose by a third, and the other fell by a quarter, and the one that fell is the more profitable business.

Booking (BKNG) vs Airbnb (ABNB): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
Booking Earns More on Every Dollar:
The operating gap between them is wider than their reputations suggest. Booking turns 34.41% of revenue into operating profit. Airbnb manages 21.01%.
That thirteen-point gap is the whole difference between the two models. Booking lists rooms somebody else built, insured, and staffed, while Airbnb has to police millions of individual hosts it does not employ.
The cash follows. Booking produced $7.73 billion of levered free cash flow against $3.21 billion at Airbnb. Earnings grew 117.90% at Booking in the most recent quarter, which is not the profile of a business in decline.
DON'T MISS: Amazon (AMZN) and Apple (AAPL) Must Face a UK Class Action Over Marketplace Sales
Airbnb Grows Faster and Owes Nothing:
Here is what the share prices have been responding to. Airbnb grew revenue 16.50% in the most recent quarter against 8.10% at Booking. For investors paying for growth rather than for margin, that is the number that matters.
The balance sheets are a genuine contrast. Airbnb holds $12.07 billion of cash against $2.50 billion of debt, so its enterprise value of $78.62 billion sits well below its market value of $88.19 billion. Booking is the other way round, with $20.92 billion of debt against $17.21 billion of cash.
Airbnb also earns 34.54% on equity, which is a strong figure and reflects how little capital the business needs. The supply is the difference nobody can copy quickly. Airbnb's inventory is millions of homes that no hotel chain owns, and no competitor can simply build.
Booking is the cheaper of the two and one of the few large travel names trading below the market multiple. You can find more of them here.
The Valuation Case:
Sustainability sits with Booking. Hotel commissions recur because hotels have no better way to fill empty rooms, and the business has survived every attempt to disintermediate it.
Airbnb's growth is faster, but its supply is individual hosts, who are more easily tempted elsewhere than a hotel chain with a distribution contract.
On price, the gap is stark. Booking trades at 13.28 times forward estimates against 25.38 times for Airbnb, so an investor pays roughly half as much for each dollar of next year's profit.
The PEG ratio settles whether that discount is deserved. Booking's is 0.61 and Airbnb's is 1.42, which means the cheaper stock is cheap even after adjusting for its slower growth. We ranked the alternatives here.
Conclusion:
Booking is the better of the two. It earns a wider margin, produces more than twice the free cash flow, trades at little more than half the forward multiple, and has fallen a quarter while its earnings more than doubled last quarter. However, Airbnb is growing twice as fast and carries net cash rather than net debt. It also owns supply that cannot be recreated. An investor choosing Booking is being paid to accept slower growth, which on these multiples looks like the better trade.

Airbnb is evolving in two directions: On the ground, it wants to compete with hotels by providing myriad services; online, it is using AI and people in its Airbnb network to aid travel discovery.

Operational Differentiation and Network Insulation
Airbnb, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ABNB) operational model relies on a highly fragmented, non-standardized supply base that inherently resists simple aggregation. Unlike traditional online travel agencies that distribute uniform hotel rooms through centralized global distribution systems, the company offers over 9 million active listings managed directly by private hosts. Standardizing or crawling millions of independent property listings, house rules, pricing algorithms, and individual host communications presents a significant hurdle for autonomous AI booking agents.
In addition, the company's direct traffic profile remains among the strongest in the digital consumer space, with nearly 90% of traffic coming direct or organically. The direct consumer relationship insulates the business from rising search engine marketing costs while posting a 35% adjusted EBITDA margin in the second quarter
Valuation, Relative Premium, and Downside Risks
Trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of roughly 25.4x, Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) carries a significant valuation premium over the broader sector median of 14.55x. While the premium highlights the company's superior cash conversion, strong net cash position, and dominant brand mindshare, it also creates a valuation risk if travel demand decelerates. High valuation multiples leave little margin for error if macroeconomic pressures dampen international leisure spending or if regulatory tightening across major metropolitan markets limits inventory growth. If booking growth slows, the stock's elevated multiple could face compression regardless of its competitive insulation against AI competitors.
Hedge Fund Sentiment and Bearish Positioning

(NASDAQ:ABNB) at the close of the second quarter, representing a decline from 87 funds in the prior quarter. Among those hedge funds, Harris Associates was the most prominent shareholder with around 18.86 million shares. The short seller activity remains controlled, with short interest standing at 3.50% of the float as of mid-September.
Cramer's bullish comment rests on the idea that Wall Street has mistakenly treated Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABNB) like a commoditized hotel booking engine. The company showed in recent quarters that its platform can generate strong free cash flow even during slow consumer environments. However, with the stock maintaining a noticeable premium over traditional travel peers, sustained booking expansion will be required to drive long-term upside from current price levels.

What Happened?
Shares of online accommodations platform Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) jumped 2.7% in the morning session after it introduced its 2026 fall update with AI search tools, social travel features, and new guest services. According to Airbnb's newsroom, the update adds AI search, filters, listing descriptions, and side-by-side home comparisons; a Connect feature with an interactive Travel Map for recommendations and prior stays from family and friends; and on-demand services such as meal and grocery delivery, laundry, and baby-gear rentals in select markets. Hosts also get tools including a multi-listing calendar, dynamic pricing, and AI earnings insights. Product expansions deepen engagement, but shares can still fall if investors treat the release as incremental rather than a near-term earnings catalyst.
The shares were trading at $161.20, up 2.7% from the previous close.

Muse is an attempt to move that choice into the agent. Singh and Tong's 5% to 10% case, reported by Barron's, is the scale investors are marking. It is not evidence that share has already moved. A booking completed inside Muse, rather than a referral back to Airbnb or Booking, is the test.

Airbnb (ABNB): Is ABNB’s Strong Growth Story Already Priced Into the Stock?
On August 7, 2026, Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) reported Q2 2026 results.
Revenue grew 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion, ahead of analysts' $3.57 billion estimate, while gross booking value rose 16% to $27.2 billion. Net income totaled $816 million and adjusted EBITDA reached $1.3 billion, a 35% margin, up over 100 basis points year-over-year. The company's free cash flow was $1.3 billion for the quarter and $4.8 billion over the trailing twelve months. Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to at least mid-teens and lifted the adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to at least 35.5%.
But Airbnb's latest Wall Street debate didn't start with September's target hikes. Here's why one analyst was already warning that the stock's strong fundamentals had become part of the problem.
Airbnb (ABNB): Is ABNB’s Strong Growth Story Already Priced Into the Stock?
Hotels, AI Efficiency, and Record First-Time Booker Growth are Winning Over Wall Street
Citizens analyst Matthew Condon raised his target on Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) to $200 from $190 on September 18, keeping Outperform and naming Hotels and AI-powered pricing as key catalysts through 2027. Raymond James upgraded ABNB to Outperform from Market Perform on September 8, lifting its target to $200 after a deep dive reinforcing confidence in durable low double-digit growth. Rosenblatt's Scott Devitt initiated coverage on September 1 with a Buy rating and a $220 target, the highest of the four, arguing focus is shifting toward new businesses starting to show results.
The quarter supported that view.
Nights and seats booked grew 10%, an acceleration from Q1, and app bookings rose 23%, now 64% of total nights booked. First-time bookers grew 11%, the fastest pace in four years, led by Gen Z, while expansion markets grew roughly twice as fast as core markets. Management credited an AI overhaul of search, checkout, and pricing for cutting support costs per booking by 16%. Hotels remain a single-digit share of nights booked but are growing about three times faster than core rentals, and CEO Brian Chesky said host interest has recently surged.
One Analyst Thinks the Good News is Already Priced In, and the Stock's Own Reaction Agrees
Morgan Stanley assumed coverage on September 16 with an Equal Weight rating and a $170 target, the lowest of the four, arguing shares already fully embed low double-digit room night growth and margin expansion through 2028. The stock's performance supports that reading: a company beating and raising guidance across every metric has still lost roughly a fifth of its value in a month.
Some caution traces to capital allocation.
On September 14, Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) announced a $250 million Housing Accelerator program, starting with a roughly 200-unit development in Austin. Chesky framed it as getting ahead of housing affordability criticism, and management said returns will run below market rates, doing little for near-term profitability and potentially inviting more regulatory scrutiny.
Hedge funds holding long Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) positions fell to 75 from 87 in Q2, though some added meaningfully: AQR Capital increased its stake 33% to 10,624,015 shares worth $1.52 billion, and Holocene Advisors grew its position 147% to 1,951,914 shares worth $279.3 million. Harris Associates, the largest holder, trimmed 2% to 18,861,551 shares worth $2.7 billion.
Short interest rose to 14.23 million shares as of August 31 from 12.91 million a month earlier.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) trades at 25.38x forward earnings as of September 24, nearly double Booking Holdings' 13.28x, leaving little cushion if Hotels or AI monetization disappoint.
Four analysts raised targets this month on accelerating core growth, a fast-growing Hotels segment, and visible AI cost savings, yet the stock moved directly against that consensus.
Morgan Stanley's more guarded call, the only one not to raise its target into the $200s, indicates growth and margin expansion are already priced in.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) likely needs Hotels to keep scaling and the housing initiative to stay a background story before the stock can catch up with the upgrades.

Booking (BKNG) vs Airbnb (ABNB): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) closed at $159.02 on October 2, and Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) at $162.43.
The two share prices are almost identical. Over the past twelve months, one of them rose by a third, and the other fell by a quarter, and the one that fell is the more profitable business.
READ ALSO: Here is Why Tripadvisor (TRIP) is a Bad Investment at Today's Price
Booking (BKNG) vs Airbnb (ABNB): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
Booking Earns More on Every Dollar:
The operating gap between them is wider than their reputations suggest. Booking turns 34.41% of revenue into operating profit. Airbnb manages 21.01%.
That thirteen-point gap is the whole difference between the two models. Booking lists rooms somebody else built, insured, and staffed, while Airbnb has to police millions of individual hosts it does not employ.
The cash follows. Booking produced $7.73 billion of levered free cash flow against $3.21 billion at Airbnb. Earnings grew 117.90% at Booking in the most recent quarter, which is not the profile of a business in decline.
DON'T MISS: Amazon (AMZN) and Apple (AAPL) Must Face a UK Class Action Over Marketplace Sales
Airbnb Grows Faster and Owes Nothing:
Here is what the share prices have been responding to. Airbnb grew revenue 16.50% in the most recent quarter against 8.10% at Booking. For investors paying for growth rather than for margin, that is the number that matters.
The balance sheets are a genuine contrast. Airbnb holds $12.07 billion of cash against $2.50 billion of debt, so its enterprise value of $78.62 billion sits well below its market value of $88.19 billion. Booking is the other way round, with $20.92 billion of debt against $17.21 billion of cash.
Airbnb also earns 34.54% on equity, which is a strong figure and reflects how little capital the business needs. The supply is the difference nobody can copy quickly. Airbnb's inventory is millions of homes that no hotel chain owns, and no competitor can simply build.
Booking is the cheaper of the two and one of the few large travel names trading below the market multiple. You can find more of them here.
The Valuation Case:
Sustainability sits with Booking. Hotel commissions recur because hotels have no better way to fill empty rooms, and the business has survived every attempt to disintermediate it.
Airbnb's growth is faster, but its supply is individual hosts, who are more easily tempted elsewhere than a hotel chain with a distribution contract.
On price, the gap is stark. Booking trades at 13.28 times forward estimates against 25.38 times for Airbnb, so an investor pays roughly half as much for each dollar of next year's profit.
The PEG ratio settles whether that discount is deserved. Booking's is 0.61 and Airbnb's is 1.42, which means the cheaper stock is cheap even after adjusting for its slower growth. We ranked the alternatives here.
Conclusion:
Booking is the better of the two. It earns a wider margin, produces more than twice the free cash flow, trades at little more than half the forward multiple, and has fallen a quarter while its earnings more than doubled last quarter. However, Airbnb is growing twice as fast and carries net cash rather than net debt. It also owns supply that cannot be recreated. An investor choosing Booking is being paid to accept slower growth, which on these multiples looks like the better trade.
Market Sentiment:
Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) was held by 92 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $6.43 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is down from 95 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $6.63 billion in the previous quarter.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) was held by 75 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $5.37 billion at the end of the same quarter. This is down from 87 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $5.21 billion three months earlier.

Stocktwits Wall Street Wrap: Analysts Turn Bullish On Sweetgreen, Target And Airbnb – Liquidia And FICO Face Downgrades
The changes reflect new views on restaurant demand, retail traffic, travel growth, drug risks and competition in financial data.
Shoppers walk past the entrance to a Target store in Washington, DC.(Photo by Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
Wells Fargo upgraded Sweetgreen and raised its price target, citing easing Cyclospora concerns and improving traffic.
HSBC upgraded Target, while KeyBanc raised Airbnb on durable growth and hotel expansion potential.
Wells Fargo and BTIG downgraded Liquidia after a court found Yutrepia infringed United Therapeutics patents.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Six stocks are drawing fresh attention after Wall Street analysts changed their views on everything from restaurant traffic and retail demand to travel growth, patent risks and credit-score competition. Sweetgreen Inc. (SG), Target Corp. (TGT) and Airbnb Inc. (ABNB) received upgrades, while Liquidia Corp. (LQDA), Sea Ltd. (SE) and Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) faced downgrades or sharply lower price targets.
Cyclospora Concerns Ease As Sweetgreen Traffic Shows Signs Of Recovery
Wells Fargo upgraded Sweetgreen to ‘Overweight’ from ‘Equal Weight’ and lifted its price target to $11 from $6 after discussions with management. The firm said concerns tied to the Cyclospora outbreak appear to be easing, while Sweetgreen’s operational changes are starting to show results.
Wells Fargo said Sweetgreen was not responsible for the Cyclospora incident, but the episode hurt demand across the salad category. The company now sees customer traffic improving, while the analyst expects management could rely more on pricing to help absorb higher costs.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Sweetgreen shares have fallen 80% from their November 2024 peak, but improving traffic, new wraps and the end of the Cyclospora outbreak could support a recovery. Sweetgreen stock has gained over 5% so far this week and is on track for a fourth week of gains.
HSBC Turns Bullish On Target, Airbnb Could Grow Beyond Core Rentals
HSBC upgraded Target to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ and raised its price target to $190 from $125. Analyst Joe Thomas pointed to the retailer’s Q2 performance as evidence that customer visits are improving and that its turnaround efforts are gaining traction. HSBC also sees room for earnings to surpass current expectations.
KeyBanc upgraded Airbnb to ‘Overweight’ from ‘Sector Weight’ and set a $191 price target. Analyst Sergio Segura said Airbnb’s main business continues to grow steadily, while hotel bookings could become a new source of growth.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
While Target stock was down 0.4% this week, Airbnb stock has gained nearly 2%.
Yutrepia Patent Dispute Creates Fresh Uncertainty For Liquidia
Wells Fargo downgraded Liquidia to ‘Equal Weight’ from ‘Overweight’ and slashed its target to $30 from $108. The firm cited greater uncertainty for the company after a court ruling and expressed limited confidence that Liquidia will prevail on appeal.
A Delaware judge ruled that Liquidia’s Yutrepia infringes two United Therapeutics (UTHR) patent claims. Both offer inhaled treprostinil treatments for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and PH-ILD . United sells Tyvaso products, while Liquidia’s Yutrepia, approved in 2025, is a dry-powder competitor. The disputed patent covers using inhaled treprostinil to improve exercise ability in PH-ILD patients.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
BTIG separately lowered Liquidia to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Buy’, citing that the judgment could potentially halt Yutrepia across indications until the pulmonary hypertension indication is removed from its label. Liquidia stock is on track for its worst week ever with a 59% crash.
DBS Bank Cuts Sea Rating While BofA Flags Risks For FICO
DBS Bank downgraded Sea to ‘Hold’ from ‘Buy’ and cut its price target to $105 from $148. The firm said Shopee is gaining strength but higher spending is hurting margins. It also faces competition from PDD’s cross-border business and Shopee’s push into quick commerce.
BofA moved Fair Isaac to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Buy’ and cut its price target to $700 from $1,400 after the Federal Housing Finance Agency placed VantageScore 4.0 and Classic FICO on the same loan-pricing adjustment framework. BofA said the change could encourage lenders to consider VantageScore more widely, creating additional risks for FICO’s pricing, volume and market share.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Sea stock is heading for a fifth straight week of losses, with a 4.3% decline, while Fair Isaac stock is down 23% and is on track for its worst month since March.
So far this year, SG, TGT and ABNB stocks gained between 18% and 60%, while LQDA, SE and FICO stocks crashed between 18% and 60%

Central America and the CaribbeanPuerto RicoPuerto RicoRincon
As a particularly cold-blooded East Coaster, my travels are almost always to slices of paradise wrapped up in sunshine and balmy air. This year, the girls trip finally made it out of the group chat and to the oasis of Puerto Rico. It came to fruition after a period of profound change and grief for my friend group, when being together felt especially important.
Rincón retreat with a pool and ocean views
The drive from Aguadilla airport to the laid-back town of Rincón began to melt away our worries,
Lush island foliage provided privacy and peace of mind around the pool
and by the time we pulled into our peaceful little Rincon Surf Club Airbnb, we could breathe a sigh of relief. I was overjoyed that the balcony with the hammock chair we saw in the listing images was ours, so I could start each morning bright and early with a cup of coffee and a blistering sunrise. I was ready to relinquish some of my overzealous New York City tendencies to really feel the benefits of Rincón’s slower, more fluid pace. After a seamless check-in, the first thing on our minds was a dip in the crystal-clear pool which we shared with a few other neighboring properties. With our swimsuits on and a celebratory drink in hand, we preemptively planned out the week ahead, taking into account all the communal space around the pool to eat dinner, play games, and take naps in the hammock.
Our local expert and good friend James was living nearby, right in the heart of Rincón. He prepared a laundry list of ideas for things to do, including the lively Art Walk in the town square and a burlesque show at Roots Restaurant to end our week with a bang. Our Airbnb was just a short 10-15 minute drive to the center of town and all the nearby beaches. Most of our days were spent parked either at home lounging in the pool or at Playa Doña Lala beach for optimal sun and sand. The home had plenty of communal items on hand to make our time more fun, like snorkelling gear, beach chairs, umbrellas, and yoga mats. This came particularly in handy when we signed up for a yoga class on a nearby horse farm at West Coast Ecuestre. Nothing could prepare us for the kind of stillness that settles in when we were high up on a platform surrounded by trees, listening to the distant thunder of galloping horses and the sweet sound of children’s laughter.
The Airbnb's communal gear was stocked and easy to access.
Thrifty as New Yorkers are (or rather must be), we cooked most of our meals with the help of the property’s excellent kitchen setup. They had all the tools we needed to make pasta dinners, tacos, sandwiches for the beach, and endless bowls of late-night cereal. On days we didn’t eat in, we enjoyed nearby places like Wake and Break for breakfast, The Beach House for lunch, and one of the island’s holy grails for dinner: Bakku. It might take a while to get a table, but the decadent Japanese-inspired island experience was well worth the wait. Standout flavors were the melt-in-your-mouth Wagyu and the imaginative smoked cocktails.
Late nights were spent in the ocean under the moon. By the end of the trip, we had a routine down pat: dinner, night swim, showers, and a restful retreat into each of our three private rooms. The primary bedroom was a space that made you want to linger. On the first night, we made a communal wardrobe in that room’s closet. It felt cozy without ever feeling cramped. The other two bedrooms were just as inviting, with enough room and storage that everyone truly had their own space within the property. The main areas were great for gathering and chatting, while our private rooms gave us space to decompress on our own. The Airbnb always felt safe, secure, and had everything we needed. Any rainy days were saved by how comfy it was—we watched home videos in the living room, took long naps in the king and queen beds, and lingered over good conversation, perfectly content to let the rain keep us inside.
There’s something uniquely fun about discovering a new place with old friends. I hardly need to go anywhere beyond my couch to have a good time with these people, but I must admit that a lovely pool, spectacular views, and a little adventure went a long way in bringing us even closer. We often fantasize about the shared land we’ll live on together one day, and this Airbnb felt like a small, beautiful preview of that dream. It gave us more than just a place to stay for the week, but a place to truly land, exhale, and explore the life we’re always talking about building together.
A hilltop hideaway in Rincón with infinity pool views, brunch worth the drive, and a surf-meets-jungle spirit.
The original reserve here was set up by Laurance Rockefeller, but it's been transformed into a luxurious modern retreat.

Airbnb adds AI search, more social features
Airbnb is evolving in two directions: On the ground, it wants to compete with hotels by providing myriad services; online, it is using AI and people in its Airbnb network to aid travel discovery.
As part of its fall product update, the company is adding services to the app it had launched last year, such as meal delivery, laundry, baby-gear rental, ski and boat rental in limited locations, and expanded grocery delivery.
The second big feature is AI search. The company has taken a cautious approach to rolling out AI features, with CEO Brian Chesky opting to stay away from a chatbot-like interface. Earlier this year, he teased the new search feature for property discovery.
Now, users can switch on a toggle to search for properties via text or voice prompts. Once you start the search, the interface will show you dynamic filters based on your preferences. For instance, if you type “baby” in the AI search filter, Airbnb will automatically show you further filters like cribs, playgrounds, or children’s books and toys.
The platform is also using AI to bring out relevant features of a property, and will let you compare properties in your wish list by way of AI-powered summaries and reviews.
“We are finally making our first foray into AI search. And what you see is just the very beginning of something. And over the coming months, we’re going to really be iterating this very quickly. It’s not hard to create AI search; it’s hard to create AI search in e-commerce when you have $100 billion going through your platform,” Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky told TechCrunch.
“Anyone can vibe-code a search function, but to do something that doesn’t kill conversion rate, that’s the hard part.”
The company is also doubling down on social features that nudge people to take more trips and book additional experiences such as food tastings and craft workshops. Last year, the app started allowing users to connect with fellow travelers and friends on its platform.
Now, travelers can look at a map based on their connections’ past or upcoming trips. When you tap on a trip, you can see where your connection stayed, and which experiences they sought out. For those conscious about their privacy, there’s an option to not share their trips with others as well.
Airbnb is also building pages about neighborhoods based on guest reviews and other sources to help travelers discover places to eat and things to do.

Priceline, Kayak, and Expedia shipped comparable tools as far back as 2023. Airbnb's differentiator is that its AI output surfaces automatically inside the standard search flow, and Chesky has promised an agentic tool in 2027.
Airbnb kept expanding beyond stays: meal and grocery delivery in Europe, laundry via Rinse, baby gear via BabyQuip in more than 60 U.S. cities from November, ski rentals in the French Alps, and boat rentals in South Florida.
Airbnb rolled out a set of consumer AI features in the U.S., including natural language search by text or voice, AI-generated filters, AI listing descriptions, and side-by-side AI property comparisons that surface automatically in search results. Hotels are excluded from the new search for now. Rivals got there first: Priceline's Penny has offered natural language search since 2023, Kayak launched AI Mode a year ago, and Expedia has shipped natural language search on Vrbo plus Property Expert and AI Comparison on Hotels.com. Airbnb's edge is integration, since the AI descriptions and comparisons appear automatically on any search rather than only inside a chatbot. CEO Brian Chesky said at Skift Global Forum this month that Airbnb is rebuilding itself as an AI native company, and pledged an agentic AI tool in 2027. Alongside the AI launch, Airbnb added an interactive travel map for sharing trips with friends and family, expanded services including meal and grocery delivery in Europe, laundry through Rinse and baby gear through BabyQuip in the U.S., ski rentals in the French Alps, and boat rentals in South Florida. New AI host tools, including better dynamic pricing and a multi-listing calendar, arrive later this fall.
